definition_zh: 出声地；大声地
definition_en: in a voice that can be heard rather than silently, or with a raised voice
core_image: 教室里一名学生站起来，把课文一字一句念出声
scene: 清晨的教室里，老师让每个人轮流把课文念出来。The teacher asked him to read the passage aloud.
sceneCN: 这里 aloud 是「出声地」（第 1 个义项：让声音发出来、别人能听见）；句意是老师让他把这段文章朗读出来。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：响亮的；大声的，是 aloud 的词根
副词：大声地，强调音量而非「出声」
名词：扬声器，由 loud 与 speaker 合成

senses.title: In an audible voice
senses.definition: using the voice so that the words are actually heard, in contrast with reading or thinking silently
senses.definitionCN: 把话说出声音来让人听见，与默读、默想相对
senses.example: The teacher asked him to read the passage aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 老师让他把这段文章朗读出来。
senses.why: The a- here is a reduced form of on, and loud supplies the sense of sound, so aloud describes speech that is on the loud side, that is, uttered rather than kept silent.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 a- 是 on 的弱化形式，loud 提供「声音」的含义，所以 aloud 指的是让声音发出来，也就是把字句说出声，而不是留在心里。

senses.title: With a raised voice
senses.definition: in a strong voice, loud enough to be heard at a distance or above other noise
senses.definitionCN: 用较大的音量说话，使远处或嘈杂中的人也能听见
senses.example: She called aloud for help when the door jammed.
senses.exampleCN: 门卡住时，她大声呼救。
senses.why: Because loud is the core of the word, aloud kept an older sense of volume; in cries and shouts it still means not merely voiced but raised.
senses.whyCN: 因为 loud 才是这个词的核心，aloud 保留了较早的音量义；在呼喊类搭配里，它不只表示「出了声」，还表示确实提高了音量。

intro.en: Aloud is a small Middle English compound of the preposition on and the adjective loud, worn down into a single word.
intro.cn: aloud 是中古英语由介词 on 与形容词 loud 合成的小词，后来磨合成一个词。

items.en: hlud meant 'making a great sound', and it is the direct ancestor of modern loud.
items.cn: hlud 意为「发出很大声响的」，是现代 loud 的直接来源。

items.en: The preposition on could mean 'in a certain manner', a use that survives in a- words such as asleep and ablaze.
items.cn: 介词 on 可表示「处于某种状态」，这一用法保留在 asleep、ablaze 等以 a- 开头的词里。

items.en: On loud was written together as aloud and came to mean 'in a loud voice, so as to be heard'.
items.cn: on loud 合写为 aloud，意思是「用听得见的声音」。

items.en: Printing and schooling fixed read aloud as the standard phrase for reading with the voice.
items.cn: 印刷与学校教育使 read aloud 成为「朗读」的固定说法。

items.en: In present use aloud mainly contrasts with silently; the older volume sense survives in cry aloud and laugh aloud.
items.cn: 现代 aloud 主要与「默读」相对；较早的音量义保留在 cry aloud、laugh aloud 里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the loud element; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs about being heard.
note.cn: 形近组共享 loud 这一成分；近义组收与「被听见」有关的副词。

entries.definition: so that others can hear, not silently
in a way that can be heard
clearly, so that each sound is heard

normalIntro.en: Aloud is simply on plus loud: sound switched on.
normalIntro.cn: aloud 就是 on 加 loud：把声音打开。

normal.en: A- plus loud, as in asleep: a state word.
normal.cn: a- 加 loud，和 asleep 一样构成状态词。

normal.en: Read aloud means the voice is on.
normal.cn: read aloud 就是让嗓子开着读。

normal.en: Thinking aloud is letting thoughts out of the mouth.
normal.cn: think aloud 是把心里的想法从嘴里放出来。

normal.en: Out loud is the everyday synonym in speech.
normal.cn: 口语里常用 out loud 表达同样的意思。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: a-LOUD.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-LOUD。

abstract.en: Picture a voice leaving the mouth and travelling across the room.
abstract.cn: 想象声音离开嘴巴，穿过教室。

abstract.en: See a silent reader and a speaking reader side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象默读者与朗读者并排而坐。

abstract.en: Hear a shout crossing a noisy street.
abstract.cn: 听见一声呼喊穿过嘈杂的街道。

examples.en: She read the letter aloud to her grandmother.
examples.cn: 她把信大声念给祖母听。

examples.en: He wondered aloud whether anyone was still inside.
examples.cn: 他出声地嘀咕，不知道还有没有人留在里面。

examples.en: The children laughed aloud at the clown.
examples.cn: 孩子们看着小丑笑出声来。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（处于）加 loud（响）：处在出声的状态，就是朗读、大声说。

root: 古英语 hlud「发出声响」给出 loud，介词 on 弱化为 a- 表示状态，二者在中古英语合成 aloud，义为「出声地」。现代用法主要与默读相对，音量义保留在 cry aloud、laugh aloud 中。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of sound being switched on splits into plain audibility and raised volume.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把声音打开」这一核心分出两支：出声让人听见，以及提高音量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reader pronouncing the words so the room can hear.
core.cn: 核心意象：朗读者把字句念出来，整个房间都听得见。

branches.en: calling for help in a crisis

intro.en: A Germanic compound, but the a- pattern it belongs to is worth learning as a family.
intro.cn: 这是日耳曼语复合词，不过它所属的 a- 构词模式值得整族记忆。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Germanic, so no Latin entries are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分属于日耳曼语，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: a device that makes sound audible

definition_zh: 字母表；字母系统
definition_en: the set of letters used for writing a language, arranged in a fixed order
core_image: 墙上挂着一张从 A 排到 Z 的字母表
scene: 幼儿园的墙上贴着一张大大的字母表，孩子们每天跟着念。The children sang the alphabet together before class.
sceneCN: 这里 alphabet 是「字母表」（第 1 个义项：一种语言全部字母的固定排列）；句意是上课前孩子们一起唱字母歌。

senses.title: The letters of a language
senses.titleCN: 字母表（全部字母的集合）
senses.definition: the complete set of letters that a written language uses
senses.definitionCN: 一种书面语言所使用的全部字母的总和
senses.example: The English alphabet has twenty-six letters.
senses.exampleCN: 英语字母表有二十六个字母。
senses.why: The word began as the names of the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta, and those two names came to stand for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是希腊头两个字母 alpha 与 beta 的名字，后来这两个名字就代表整套字母。

senses.title: A fixed ordering
senses.definition: the conventional sequence of those letters, used for listing and looking things up
senses.definitionCN: 这些字母约定俗成的先后次序，用于排列条目与查找
senses.example: Names on the list are arranged by alphabet, not by age.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上的名字按字母顺序排列，而不是按年龄。
senses.why: Because the alphabet is learned as an ordered recitation, the word also names the order itself, which is how dictionaries and indexes work.
senses.whyCN: 因为字母表是作为有次序的背诵内容学会的，所以这个词也指这套次序本身，字典与索引正是靠它编排。

intro.en: Alphabet is a rare word whose history is visible in its first two sounds.
intro.cn: alphabet 是个少见的词，它的来历就写在开头两个音里。

items.en: Alpha was the name of the first letter, borrowed from a Phoenician letter meaning 'ox'.
items.cn: alpha 是第一个字母的名称，借自腓尼基字母，原意为「牛」。

items.en: Beta named the second letter and is the source of the English word beta.
items.cn: beta 是第二个字母的名称，也是英语 beta 的来源。

items.en: The Greeks joined the two names into alphabetos, a name for the whole set of letters.
items.cn: 希腊人把两个名字连成 alphabetos，用来指整套字母。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as alphabetum, and the learned languages of Europe passed it on.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 alphabetum，欧洲的学术语言再把它传下去。

items.en: English alphabet appears in the sixteenth century and later yields alphabetical and alphabetize.
items.cn: 英语 alphabet 在十六世纪出现，后来派生出 alphabetical 与 alphabetize。

note.en: The look-alike group traces the Greek letter names; the near-meaning group contrasts writing systems.
note.cn: 形近组追溯希腊字母名；近义组对比不同的书写系统。

entries.definition: the first letter of the Greek alphabet
entries.definitionCN: 希腊字母表的第一个字母

entries.definition: the second letter of the Greek alphabet
entries.definitionCN: 希腊字母表的第二个字母

entries.definition: arranged in the order of the alphabet
any organised method of writing a language
entries.definitionCN: 书写一种语言的任何成套方法

entries.definition: the set of written characters used for a language
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言使用的整套书写符号

entries.definition: a writing system whose signs stand for syllables, not single letters
entries.definitionCN: 符号代表音节而非单个字母的书写系统

normalIntro.en: Alpha plus beta: the alphabet is named after its first two letters.
normalIntro.cn: alpha 加 beta：字母表正是用它头两个字母命名的。

normal.en: Say the first two Greek letters and you have said alphabet.
normal.cn: 念出希腊头两个字母，就说出了 alphabet。

normal.en: The English alphabet runs from A to Z.
normal.cn: 英语字母表从 A 排到 Z。

normal.en: Alphabetical adds -ical: arranged by letters.
normal.cn: alphabetical 加 -ical：按字母排列的。

normal.en: A dictionary is the alphabet put to work.
normal.cn: 字典就是让字母顺序干活。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AL-pha-bet.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AL-pha-bet。

abstract.en: Picture a wall chart from A down to Z.
abstract.cn: 想象一张从 A 排到 Z 的挂图。

abstract.en: See a child singing the letters in order.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子按顺序唱字母。

abstract.en: Imagine a library shelf sorted by first letter.
abstract.cn: 想象按首字母排好的书架。

examples.en: Children usually learn the alphabet before they can read.
examples.cn: 孩子通常先学字母表，然后才学会阅读。

examples.en: The index lists all the places in alphabet order.
examples.cn: 索引按字母顺序列出所有地点。

examples.en: Some languages use an alphabet of more than forty letters.
examples.cn: 有些语言使用的字母表包含四十多个字母。

dict_mnemonic.text: alpha 与 beta 是希腊头两个字母，把它们连起来就得到「字母表」。

root: 希腊语 alphabetos 由头两个字母名 alpha 与 beta 连成，指整套字母；拉丁语作 alphabetum，十六世纪进入英语，并派生出 alphabetical、alphabetize 等词。

sensesIntro.en: From a name for the letter set comes a second use for its fixed order.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「整套字母」的名称，又生出「这套固定次序」的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: A to Z hung on the classroom wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：从 A 到 Z 挂在教室墙上。

branches.en: the Greek letters used in science
branches.cn: 科学中使用的希腊字母

branches.en: an index built on first letters

intro.en: The word is Greek in origin, and its family grows with Latin-style suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词源自希腊语，它的词族靠拉丁式后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base alphabet- was passed through Latin, which supplies the combining forms below.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词基 alphabet- 经拉丁语传来，下面列出相关的构词成分。

items.meaning: the act of sorting by letters

definition_zh: 按字母顺序的；字母表的
definition_en: arranged according to the order of the letters of the alphabet, or relating to an alphabet
core_image: 电话簿的页面，名字从 A 一路排到 Z
scene: 前台把参会者的名牌按字母顺序摆好，方便大家快速找到自己的。The receptionist put the name cards in alphabetical order.
sceneCN: 这里 alphabetical 是「按字母顺序的」（第 1 个义项：依照字母表先后排列）；句意是前台把名牌按字母顺序摆好。

pos.zh: 形容词：按字母顺序的；字母表的

derivatives.zh: 名词：字母表，是本词的词基
形容词：字母与数字混合的

senses.title: Arranged in letter order
senses.definition: put in the sequence of the alphabet, from A towards Z
senses.definitionCN: 依照字母表从 A 到 Z 的先后排列
senses.example: The names on the register are in alphabetical order.
senses.exampleCN: 登记册上的名字按字母顺序排列。
senses.why: The suffix -ical turns alphabet into an adjective of manner, so the word says that something follows the alphabet rather than merely mentioning it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ical 把 alphabet 变成表示方式形容词，所以这个词说明某物是依照字母表排列的，而不只是提到字母表。

senses.title: Relating to an alphabet
senses.definition: connected with alphabets as writing systems, especially in contrast with picture or syllable writing
senses.definitionCN: 与作为书写系统的字母表有关，尤指区别于图画文字或音节文字
senses.example: Scholars describe the change from picture signs to alphabetical writing.
senses.exampleCN: 学者描述从图画符号到字母书写的转变。
senses.why: Because -ical also makes classifying adjectives, alphabetical can label a type of writing system, not just an order within one.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -ical 也能构成分类形容词，alphabetical 可以标示一种书写系统的类型，而不只是某系统内部的排列方式。

intro.en: Alphabetical is alphabet fitted with the Latin adjectival ending -ical.
intro.cn: alphabetical 就是 alphabet 加上拉丁形容词后缀 -ical。

items.en: The Greek name for the letter set came from alpha and beta.
items.cn: 希腊语中「整套字母」的名称来自 alpha 与 beta。

items.en: Latin kept the word as alphabetum, the base later taken into English.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留为 alphabetum，后来作为词基进入英语。

items.en: English alphabet is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 alphabet 在十六世纪有记录。

items.en: The ending -icus formed adjectives of belonging, and English -ical continues it through French and Latin models.
items.cn: 后缀 -icus 构成表示归属的形容词，英语 -ical 经法语与拉丁语模式延续了它。

items.en: Alphabetical settled into use for lists, indexes, and dictionaries arranged by letters.
items.cn: alphabetical 在十七世纪固定用于按字母排列的清单、索引与字典。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the -ical family; the near-meaning group names other ordering principles.
note.cn: 形近组展示 -ical 词族；近义组列出其他排序原则。

entries.definition: done according to an organised method
arranged by time rather than by letters
entries.definitionCN: 按时间而非字母排列的

normalIntro.en: Alphabet plus -ical: the adjective of letter order.
normalIntro.cn: alphabet 加 -ical：表示字母顺序的形容词。

normal.en: Alphabetical order is the order you learn as a child.
normal.cn: alphabetical order 就是小时候背的那套顺序。

normal.en: The -ical ending answers the question 'in what way'.
normal.cn: -ical 结尾回答「以什么方式」。

normal.en: A dictionary is the most familiar alphabetical list.
normal.cn: 字典是最熟悉的字母顺序清单。

normal.en: The adverb simply adds -ly.
normal.cn: 副词形式只是再加 -ly。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: al-pha-BET-i-cal.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：al-pha-BET-i-cal。

abstract.en: Picture a phone book running from A to Z.
abstract.cn: 想象一本从 A 排到 Z 的电话簿。

abstract.en: See files lined up by their first letter.
abstract.cn: 想象文件按首字母排成一列。

abstract.en: Imagine a shelf where A comes before B.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上 A 排在 B 前面。

examples.en: Please file these reports in alphabetical order.
examples.cn: 请把这些报告按字母顺序归档。

examples.en: The glossary is alphabetical, so finding a term is quick.
examples.cn: 词汇表按字母排列，查找术语很快。

examples.en: Her surname puts her near the front of any alphabetical list.
examples.cn: 她的姓氏让她在任何字母顺序名单里都排得靠前。

dict_mnemonic.text: alphabet（字母表）加 -ical（……的）：按字母表来的。

root: 词基 alphabet 源自希腊语 alphabetos，经拉丁语 alphabetum 进入英语；后缀 -ical 来自拉丁 -icus，构成表示方式或类属的形容词，十七世纪起用于列表与索引的编排。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective covers both the order of letters and the type of writing that uses them.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词既指字母的排列次序，也指使用字母的书写类型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone book whose pages march from A to Z.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本从 A 排到 Z 的电话簿。

branches.en: an index sorted by first letter

branches.cn: 为快速查找而排列的文件

branches.en: alphabetical writing compared with picture signs
branches.cn: 字母书写与图画符号的对比

branches.en: a script based on single letters
branches.cn: 以单个字母为基础的书写系统

intro.en: A Greek base with a Latin adjectival suffix, a typical learned formation.
intro.cn: 希腊词基配拉丁形容词后缀，是典型的学术构词。

latinIntro.en: Both the base and the suffix travelled through Latin, so the Latin entries are relevant here.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都经过拉丁语，因此这里列出相关拉丁词条。

items.meaning: the state of being in letter order
items.example: check the alphabeticality of the list

items.meaning: a system based on an alphabet
items.meaningCN: 以字母表为基础的系统

latinEntries.meaning: belonging to, of the nature of

definition_zh: 按字母顺序地
definition_en: in the order of the alphabet, from A towards Z
core_image: 手指顺着卡片盒里的分隔卡，从 A 抽到 Z
scene: 档案室新来的实习生把所有客户资料按字母顺序排了一遍。The intern filed the customer records alphabetically.
sceneCN: 这里 alphabetically 是「按字母顺序地」（第 1 个义项：依照字母表先后排列）；句意是实习生把客户资料按字母顺序归档。

senses.title: In A-to-Z order
senses.definition: following the sequence of the alphabet when arranging or naming things
senses.definitionCN: 在排列或列举事物时依照字母表的先后次序
senses.example: The books on the shelf are arranged alphabetically by author.
senses.exampleCN: 书架上的书按作者姓氏的字母顺序排列。
senses.why: The adverb is the -ly form of alphabetical, so it describes how an action such as filing, sorting, or listing is carried out, not what a thing is.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 alphabetical 的 -ly 形式，因此它说明归档、分类、列举等动作是怎样进行的，而不是说明事物本身是什么。

senses.title: By initial letter
senses.definition: using only the first letter as the basis for grouping, as in simple address books
senses.definitionCN: 只以首字母作为分组依据，如简易通讯录的做法
senses.example: For speed, the volunteers grouped the forms alphabetically rather than by date.
senses.exampleCN: 为求速度，志愿者们按首字母给表格分组，而不是按日期。
senses.why: In practice many lists never reach the second letter, so the adverb often means merely grouping under initials, a looser version of full alphabet order.
senses.whyCN: 实际使用中很多清单根本排不到第二个字母，所以这个副词常只表示按首字母分组，是完整字母顺序的宽松版本。

intro.en: Alphabetically is a three-layer word: Greek letter names, a Latin adjective, and an English adverb ending.
intro.cn: alphabetically 有三层构造：希腊字母名、拉丁形容词、英语副词词尾。

items.en: The first two Greek letter names joined to name the whole set.
items.cn: 希腊头两个字母名连起来，用来指整套字母。

items.en: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century through Latin.
items.cn: 这个名词在十六世纪经拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective with -ical appeared in the seventeenth century for lists and indexes.
items.cn: 带 -ical 的形容词在十七世纪出现，用于清单与索引。

items.en: The native adverb ending -ly was added to the adjective to form alphabetically.
items.cn: 英语本族副词词尾 -ly 加在形容词上，构成 alphabetically。

items.en: Modern filing, libraries, and computers made the word an everyday instruction: sort alphabetically.
items.cn: 现代档案、图书馆与计算机使这个词成为日常指令：按字母排序。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same family; the near-meaning group offers other sorting adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组属于同一词族；近义组给出其他排序方式副词。

normalIntro.en: Alphabetical plus -ly: the adverb of A-to-Z sorting.
normalIntro.cn: alphabetical 加 -ly：A 到 Z 排序的副词。

normal.en: If the action follows the alphabet, use alphabetically.
normal.cn: 动作依照字母表进行，就用 alphabetically。

normal.en: Sort alphabetically is the standard filing instruction.
normal.cn: sort alphabetically 是标准的归档指令。

normal.en: The -ly tells you it describes a verb.

definition_zh: 已经；早已；（用于疑问或惊讶）竟然已经
definition_en: before now or before a particular time, often sooner than expected
core_image: 餐桌上空了的碗，客人还没到主人就吃完了
scene: 妈妈端着汤走进餐厅，发现孩子已经把饭吃完，碗都收好了。The boy has already finished his dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 already 是「已经」（第 1 个义项：在某时间点之前就完成）；句意是男孩已经把晚饭吃完了。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：准备好的，是 already 的词根来源
短语：全都准备好了，与 already 常被混用

senses.title: Before now, sooner than expected
senses.definition: used with a past or perfect tense to say that something happened before the present moment, often earlier than expected
senses.definitionCN: 与过去时或完成时连用，表示某事在当前时刻之前就发生了，常含早于预期之意
senses.example: The boy has already finished his dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩已经把晚饭吃完了。
senses.why: The word grew out of all ready, meaning fully prepared, so already signals that a stage is not merely reached but completely behind us.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 all ready「完全准备好」演变而来，因此 already 表示某个阶段不仅到了，而且已经彻底走完，落在我们身后。

senses.title: By a given past time
senses.definition: used in past perfect sentences to mark that an action was complete before another past event
senses.definitionCN: 用于过去完成时，标示某动作在另一个过去事件之前就已完成
senses.example: By the time we arrived, the train had already left.
senses.exampleCN: 我们赶到时，火车已经开走了。
senses.why: Because already points to completion, it pairs naturally with had to set one past event behind another, giving the sentence a clear before-and-after order.
senses.whyCN: 因为 already 指向完成状态，它天然与 had 搭配，把一个过去事件置于另一个之前，让句子有清楚的先后次序。

senses.title: Surprise in a question
senses.definition: used in questions or exclamations to show surprise that something has happened so soon
senses.definitionCN: 用于疑问句或感叹句，表示对某事发生得如此之快感到惊讶
senses.example: Are you leaving already?
senses.exampleCN: 你这就要走了吗？
senses.why: In questions the expectation built into already turns into disbelief, so the same word can carry surprise rather than simple timing.
senses.whyCN: 在疑问句里，already 内含的「早于预期」变成了难以置信，所以同一个词可以表达惊讶，而不只是陈述时间。

intro.en: Already is a worn-down phrase, not a root: it began as all ready.
intro.cn: already 不是词根词，而是一个磨掉了形状的短语，最初写作 all ready。

items.en: eall meant 'the whole of, entirely', the ancestor of modern all.
items.cn: eall 意为「全部、完全」，是现代 all 的前身。

items.en: ræde meant 'prepared, ready', and it survives in the adjective ready.
items.cn: ræde 意为「准备好的」，保存在形容词 ready 中。

items.en: The two words were written as a phrase meaning 'fully ready', then fused into one word.
items.cn: 两个词先写作短语，意为「完全就绪」，随后合并成一个词。

items.en: Already acquired its modern time sense: completed before the moment of speaking.
items.cn: already 在十四世纪获得现代的时间义：在说话时刻之前已完成。

items.en: The older phrase all ready still exists separately, so the two spellings now contrast.
items.cn: 较早的短语 all ready 仍独立存在，于是两种拼写现在形成对照。

note.en: The look-alike group warns about the split phrase; the near-meaning group compares time adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组提醒分词短语的区别；近义组比较时间副词。

sensesIntro.en: The core idea of complete readiness yields three uses: before now, before a past point, and surprise at speed.

definition_zh: 也；还；而且
definition_en: in addition to something already mentioned, or in the same way
core_image: 两份并列的清单，第二份多出一行
scene: 面试官翻着简历，说她会法语，还会德语和西班牙语。She speaks French and also German.
sceneCN: 这里 also 是「也；还」（第 1 个义项：在已提到的事物之外再加一项）；句意是她会法语，还会德语。

derivatives.zh: 副词：这样；如此，是 also 的词源成分之一

senses.title: In addition
senses.definition: used to add another item, fact, or action to what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 在刚说过的话之外再补充一项内容、事实或动作
senses.example: She speaks French and also German.
senses.exampleCN: 她会说法语，还会德语。
senses.why: The word descends from all so, meaning 'quite so', and that sense of adding the same again became the modern additive use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自 all so「完全如此」，这种「再同样来一遍」的意味发展成现代表示补充的用法。

senses.title: In the same way
senses.definition: used to say that the same statement is true of another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 表示同样的说法也适用于另一个人或另一件事
senses.example: I think the plan is risky, and my colleague also thinks so.
senses.exampleCN: 我认为这个计划有风险，我同事也这么想。
senses.why: When the added item is not a new fact but the same judgement applied to someone else, also shifts from addition to agreement.
senses.whyCN: 当补充的不是新事实，而是把同一个判断套到别人身上时，also 就从「增加」转为「同样如此」。

intro.en: Also is an old compound of all and so that has kept its additive meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: also 是 all 与 so 的古老复合词，一千年间保持了「附加」的含义。

items.en: eall meant 'wholly, entirely', the source of modern all.
items.cn: eall 意为「完全、全部」，是现代 all 的来源。

items.en: swa meant 'so, in that way', the ancestor of so.
items.cn: swa 意为「如此、以那种方式」，是 so 的前身。

items.en: ealswa meant 'quite so, just so', and it was used to add a matching item.
items.cn: ealswa 意为「正是如此」，用来补充一个相配的项目。

items.en: The form shrank to also, and its additive sense became standard in writing.
items.cn: 词形缩为 also，其补充义在书面语中成为标准。

items.en: Modern grammars place also before the main verb, unlike too at the end of a clause.
items.cn: 现代语法要求 also 放在主要动词之前，与置于句末的 too 不同。

note.cn: 形近组区分短小虚词；近义组比较表示追加的副词。

root: 源自古英语 ealswa，由 eall「全部」与 swa「如此」合成，义为「完全如此」，中古英语缩为 also，保留「在原有内容之外再加一项」的核心义。

definition_zh: 改变；更改；（把衣服）改小或改大
definition_en: to change something, or to become different, often in a partial way
core_image: 裁缝把一条过长的裤脚卷起、重新缝好
scene: 裁缝量了量裤脚，说可以改短两厘米，明天就能取。The tailor altered the trousers to fit me.
sceneCN: 这里 alter 是「改（衣服）」（第 3 个义项：通过缝改使衣物合身）；句意是裁缝把裤子改得合我的身。

derivatives.zh: 名词：替代方案，与 alter 同源

senses.title: To change something partly
senses.definition: to make something different, usually by changing part of it rather than replacing it entirely
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得不同，通常是改动其中一部分，而不是整体替换
senses.example: The new evidence altered the course of the investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据改变了调查的方向。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin alter, 'the other of two', so to alter is to make a thing other than it was, a shift rather than a total replacement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」，所以 alter 是让事物变成与原来不同的另一个样子，是转变而不是整体替换。

senses.title: To become different
senses.definition: to change by itself over time, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 自身随时间发生变化，不带宾语
senses.example: Her expression altered when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，她的表情变了。
senses.why: Because the change can happen without an agent, the verb also works intransitively, describing a state that shifts rather than someone acting on it.
senses.whyCN: 因为变化可以在没有施动者的情况下发生，这个动词也可作不及物用法，描述状态自身发生转变。

senses.title: To adjust clothing
senses.definition: to take in or let out a garment so that it fits better
senses.definitionCN: 把衣服收小或放宽，使其更合身
senses.example: The tailor altered the trousers to fit me.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝把裤子改得合我的身。
senses.why: Tailoring is change on a small scale: the garment stays the same object but its measurements are made other, which is exactly the Latin sense in daily use.
senses.whyCN: 裁缝做的就是小尺度改动：衣服还是那件衣服，只是尺寸被改成另一个样子，这正是 alter 的拉丁本义在日常中的体现。

intro.en: Alter goes back to a Latin word for 'the other of two', which explains why it means change rather than replace.
intro.cn: alter 可追溯到拉丁语「两者中的另一个」，这解释了它为何意为改变而非替换。

items.en: alter meant 'the other one of two', as in alter ego, a second self.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，如 alter ego 指第二个自我。

items.en: The verb alterare meant 'to make other, to change'.
items.cn: 动词 alterare 意为「使成为另一个、改变」。

items.en: French passed the verb on as alterer, used for changing plans, words, or goods.
items.cn: 法语以 alterer 传下这个动词，用于改变计划、言辞或货物。

items.en: English alter appears in the fourteenth century with the sense 'to make different'.
items.cn: 英语 alter 在十四世纪出现，意为「使不同」。

items.en: The clothing sense grew from everyday tailoring, while alteration names any change made.
items.cn: 衣物义从日常裁缝发展而来，而 alteration 泛指任何改动。

note.cn: 形近组区分同音词 altar；近义组按改动方式分级。

examples.en: His mood altered as soon as the rain stopped.

definition_zh: 可供替代的；非传统的；替代方案；选择
definition_en: another possibility instead of the usual one, or a choice between two or more things
core_image: 岔路口立着两块路牌，一块指向老路，一块指向新路
scene: 医生建议先休息，如果还疼再考虑别的方案，比如物理治疗。The doctor suggested an alternative treatment.
sceneCN: 这里 alternative 是「可供替代的」（第 1 个义项：在常规办法之外另有一种可选做法）；句意是医生建议了一种替代疗法。

pos.zh: 形容词：可供替代的；非传统的

derivatives.zh: 副词：或者；作为另一种选择
动词：改变，与 alternative 同源

senses.title: Another possible choice
senses.titleCN: 可供替代的；另一可选的
senses.definition: available as another possibility in place of the usual or first one
senses.definitionCN: 作为常规或首选之外的另一可能而存在
senses.example: We need an alternative route because the bridge is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 桥封了，我们需要另一条路线。
senses.why: The Latin base alter means 'the other of two', and -native makes an adjective of offering, so alternative describes what stands ready as the other choice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，-native 构成表示「提供」的形容词，所以 alternative 指作为另一个选择随时可用的方案。

senses.title: Outside the mainstream
senses.definition: deliberately different from the dominant or conventional system, as in alternative medicine or energy
senses.definitionCN: 有意区别于主流或传统体系，如替代医学、替代能源
senses.example: Some patients turn to alternative medicine when drugs fail.
senses.exampleCN: 有些病人在药物无效时转向替代疗法。
senses.why: Twentieth-century counterculture gave the word a second edge: the alternative is not merely another option but a rejection of the established one.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪的反主流文化给这个词添了第二层锋芒：alternative 不只是另一个选项，还带有对既定做法的拒绝。

senses.title: A choice to be made
senses.definition: one of two or more things that can be chosen, especially when the first is unsatisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个可选事物之一，尤指首选不理想时的备选
senses.example: The committee saw no alternative but to cancel the event.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会别无选择，只能取消活动。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the second path itself, and the common phrase no alternative shows how it carries the weight of a forced decision.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词指第二条路本身，常见说法 no alternative 正体现它承载着「被迫决断」的分量。

intro.en: Alternative is built on the Latin idea of 'the other of two', later widened to any option and finally to anti-mainstream choices.
intro.cn: alternative 建立在拉丁语「两者中的另一个」之上，后来扩为任何选项，最终又指反主流的选择。

items.en: alter meant 'the other of two', the root also seen in alter ego.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，也见于 alter ego。

items.en: alternare meant 'to do one thing then the other, to alternate'.
items.cn: alternare 意为「轮流做一件事和另一件事」。

items.en: French formed alternatif for a choice that offers one thing or the other.
items.cn: 法语构成 alternatif，指非此即彼的选择。

items.en: English alternative first described a choice between two possibilities.
items.cn: 英语 alternative 最初描述两种可能之间的取舍。

items.en: The modern sense of alternative energy or medicine marks a deliberate move away from the mainstream.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现的 alternative energy、alternative medicine 表示有意离开主流。

note.en: The look-alike group separates alter, alternate, and alternative; the near-meaning group names kinds of options.
note.cn: 形近组区分 alter、alternate 与 alternative；近义组列出各类选项。

normal.cn: alternative 与 alternate 都来自 alter。

normal.en: Alternative medicine stands outside the mainstream.

abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里放着备用的 B 计划。

examples.cn: 骑车上班是开车之外的健康选择。

examples.cn: 议会正在寻找替代能源。

examples.cn: 我们别无选择，只能等下一班火车。

root: 源自拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」及动词 alternare「轮流」，经法语 alternatif 于十六世纪进入英语，先指二者择一，二十世纪又发展出「非主流、另类」的义项。

intro.en: A Latin root with a French-Latin suffix, plus a cluster of look-alike forms.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根配法拉丁后缀，并带一串形近词。

latinIntro.en: The base alter and the verb alternare are both Latin, so they are listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 alter 与动词 alternare 都是拉丁语，列在下面。

definition_zh: 或者；作为另一种选择；（提出另一种解释）也可能
definition_en: used to introduce another possibility, either a different course of action or a different explanation
core_image: 写到一半的方案页边，用铅笔补了一条「或者」
scene: 出发前她看了看天气，说可以坐地铁，或者干脆改天再去。We could go now; alternatively, we could wait until tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 alternatively 是「或者」（第 1 个义项：提出另一条可选的做法）；句意是我们现在可以去，或者等到明天。

pos.zh: 副词：或者；作为另一种选择

derivatives.zh: 形容词：可供替代的；名词：替代方案
动词：改变，是本词的远源词根

senses.title: As another course of action
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to offer a different action that could be taken instead
senses.definitionCN: 置于分句开头，提出可以改做的另一件事
senses.example: We could walk; alternatively, we could take the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以走过去，或者坐公交。
senses.why: The adverb is alternative turned into a sentence connector, so it points from the action just named to the other action on offer.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 alternative 变来的句子连接词，作用是从刚提到的做法指向另一个可选做法。

senses.title: As another explanation
senses.titleCN: 也可能是；另一种解释是
senses.definition: used to offer a second possible explanation for the same facts
senses.definitionCN: 针对同样的事实提出第二种可能的解释
senses.example: The delay may be due to traffic; alternatively, the driver may be lost.
senses.exampleCN: 延误可能是堵车，也可能是司机迷路了。
senses.why: The same connector works for ideas as well as actions: when the alternatives are explanations rather than plans, it introduces a rival account of the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个连接词同样可用于想法而不只是行动：当备选项是解释而不是计划时，它引出对同一证据的另一种说法。

intro.en: Alternatively is a nineteenth-century adverb built on alternative, which itself rests on the Latin word for 'the other of two'.
intro.cn: alternatively 是十九世纪由 alternative 构成的副词，而 alternative 又建立在拉丁语「两者中的另一个」之上。

items.en: alter meant 'the other of two', the base of the whole family.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，是整族词的词基。

items.en: French alternatif described a choice offering one thing or the other.
items.cn: 法语 alternatif 指非此即彼的选择。

items.en: English alternative entered in the sixteenth century as an adjective and noun of choice.
items.cn: 英语 alternative 于十六世纪进入，作表示选择的形容词与名词。

items.en: The adverb alternatively appears as a formal way to open a second clause.
items.cn: 副词 alternatively 在十九世纪出现，作为开启第二个分句的正式说法。

items.en: Today it is the standard written connector for a second option or a second explanation.
items.cn: 如今它是书面语中引出第二选项或第二种解释的标准连接词。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts alternative and alternately; the near-meaning group gives rival connectors.
note.cn: 形近组对比 alternative 与 alternately；近义组给出同类连接词。

normalIntro.en: Alternative plus -ly: the connector that opens the other path.
normalIntro.cn: alternative 加 -ly：打开另一条路的连接词。

normal.en: It opens a clause, usually after a semicolon or full stop.
normal.cn: 它开启一个分句，前面常用分号或句号。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with alternately, which means in turns.
normal.cn: 别和 alternately 混了，后者意为交替地。

normal.en: Alternatively works for plans and for explanations.
normal.cn: alternatively 既能引出计划，也能引出解释。

normal.en: Or alternatively is a common spoken doubling.
normal.cn: 口语里常说 or alternatively。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: al-TER-na-tive-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：al-TER-na-tive-ly。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil note in the margin: or this.
abstract.cn: 想象页边用铅笔写着「或者这样」。

abstract.en: See two doors side by side, only one open.
abstract.cn: 想象并排两扇门，只有一扇开着。

abstract.en: Hear a second explanation offered after the first.
abstract.cn: 听到在第一个解释之后又给出第二个。

examples.en: You can pay online; alternatively, send a cheque by post.
examples.cn: 你可以在线支付，或者邮寄支票。

examples.en: The noise could come from the pipes; alternatively, it might be the neighbours.
examples.cn: 噪音可能来自管道，也可能是邻居。

examples.en: Alternatively, we could hold the meeting on Friday.
examples.cn: 或者，我们可以把会议改到周五。

dict_mnemonic.text: alternative（另一个选择）加 -ly：以「另一个选择」的方式说话，就是「或者」。

root: 由 alternative 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，alternative 源自拉丁 alter「两者中的另一个」与 alternare「轮流」，经法语进入英语；十九世纪起 alternatively 用作书面连接词，引出另一做法或另一解释。

sensesIntro.en: One connector serves two kinds of alternatives: a different action and a different explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个连接词服务两类备选：另一种做法与另一种解释。

intro.en: A Latin-rooted adjective turned adverb, common in formal writing.
intro.cn: 这是拉丁词根的形容词变来的副词，常见于正式书面语。

latinIntro.en: The root alter and the verb alternare supply the Latin background.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 alter 与动词 alternare 提供拉丁语背景。

definition_zh: 尽管；虽然；不过
definition_en: used to introduce a fact that contrasts with the main statement, or to add a limiting remark after it
core_image: 一个人撑着伞站在雨里，却笑得很开心
scene: 外面下着大雨，他还是按时到了集合点，只是鞋子全湿了。Although it was raining, he arrived on time.
sceneCN: 这里 although 是「尽管」（第 1 个义项：引出一个与主句相反的事实）；句意是尽管下着雨，他还是准时到了。

derivatives.zh: 连词：虽然，是 although 的简略同义词
短语：即使；尽管，语气更强
副词：完全，是 although 的构词成分

senses.title: Despite the fact that
senses.definition: used at the beginning of a clause to admit a fact that makes the main statement surprising
senses.definitionCN: 置于分句开头，先承认一个使主句显得意外的事实
senses.example: Although it was raining, he arrived on time.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下着雨，他还是准时到了。
senses.why: The word is all plus though, literally 'even though', and the all strengthens the concession: the whole of the opposing fact is granted before the main point.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 all 与 though 合成，字面是「即使如此」，all 加强了让步：先把相反的事实整个承认下来，再说主句。

senses.title: A trailing qualification
senses.titleCN: 不过；只是（句末补充限制）
senses.definition: used after the main statement to add a fact that limits or qualifies it
senses.definitionCN: 用在主句之后，补充一个限制或削弱前述内容的事实
senses.example: The plan is sensible, although it will cost a lot.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划是合理的，不过花费会很大。
senses.why: Because the concession can come second, although also works as a soft but, letting a speaker agree first and add the objection afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 因为让步内容也可以放在后面，although 还能起温和的「但是」作用，让人先表示同意，再补上异议。

intro.en: Although is a Middle English compound of all and though, and the all is there to make the concession complete.
intro.cn: although 是中古英语 all 与 though 的复合词，其中的 all 用来把让步说满。

items.en: eall meant 'wholly, entirely', the source of modern all.
items.cn: eall 意为「完全、全部」，是现代 all 的来源。

items.en: þeah meant 'though, nevertheless', the ancestor of though.
items.cn: þeah 意为「虽然、然而」，是 though 的前身。

items.en: The phrase al thogh meant 'even though' and was written as two words.
items.cn: 短语 al thogh 意为「即使如此」，当时写作两个词。

items.en: The two parts fused into although and settled at the head of a concessive clause.
items.cn: 两部分合并为 although，固定在让步从句的开头。

items.en: Modern usage allows although at the head of a sentence or after the main clause, but not as a bare final adverb.
items.cn: 现代用法允许 although 位于句首或主句之后，但不能像 though 那样单独放在句末作副词。

note.en: The look-alike group separates although from though and thought; the near-meaning group lists concessive connectors.
note.cn: 形近组区分 although、though 与 thought；近义组列出让步连接词。

an idea, or the past of think

normalIntro.en: All plus though: grant the whole opposing fact, then say the main point.
normalIntro.cn: all 加 though：先把相反的事实整个认下，再说主句。

normal.en: Although cannot stand alone at the end like though.

abstract.en: Hear agreement first, objection second.
abstract.cn: 听到先同意、后补充异议。

examples.cn: 尽管考试很难，大多数学生还是通过了。

examples.en: She kept working, although she was clearly tired.

examples.en: Although small, the room is bright and quiet.

root: 源自古英语 eall「全部」与 þeah「虽然」，中古英语写作 al thogh，十四世纪合并为 although，核心是先把相反事实完整承认，再给出主句。

sensesIntro.en: The concession can come first or last, giving a leading although and a trailing one.
sensesIntro.cn: 让步内容可以放前也可以放后，于是有前置的 although 与句末补充的 although。

definition_zh: 海拔；高度；（几何中的）高
definition_en: the height of a place above sea level, height in general, or the perpendicular height of a geometric figure
core_image: 飞机舷窗外的雪山，仪表盘上标着飞行高度
scene: 飞机爬升到巡航高度后，窗外的河流变成了一条细线。The plane reached a cruising altitude of ten thousand metres.
sceneCN: 这里 altitude 是「高度」（第 2 个义项：物体离地面的垂直距离）；句意是飞机达到了一万米的巡航高度。

derivatives.zh: 名词：高原，与 altitude 同源于「高」
名词：中音；高音，源自拉丁语「高」

senses.title: Height above sea level
senses.definition: the vertical distance of a place above the level of the sea, used in geography and travel
senses.definitionCN: 某地高出海平面的垂直距离，用于地理与旅行
senses.example: The village sits at an altitude of three thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄位于海拔三千米处。
senses.why: Latin altitudo came from altus, 'high', and in geography the word was fixed to the one reference line that matters, the sea.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 altitudo 来自 altus「高的」，在地理中这个词被固定到唯一重要的基准线，也就是海平面。

senses.title: Height above the ground
senses.definition: the height of an aircraft or object above the ground or a chosen level at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 飞机或物体在某一时刻离地面或某一基准的高度
senses.example: The plane reached a cruising altitude of ten thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机达到了一万米的巡航高度。
senses.why: Once the word meant height in general, aviation could use it for a changing measurement rather than a fixed spot on the map.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本泛指高度，航空便用它表示不断变化的测量值，而不是地图上固定的地点。

senses.title: Perpendicular height of a figure
senses.definition: the line drawn at right angles from a vertex to the opposite side of a triangle or solid
senses.definitionCN: 从顶点垂直画到对边的线段，用于三角形或立体图形
senses.example: The area of a triangle is half the base times the altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形的面积等于底乘高的一半。
senses.why: Geometry kept the pure sense of 'height' and gave it a precise meaning: the perpendicular distance from a vertex to the opposite side.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了「高度」的纯粹含义，并给它精确定义：从顶点到对边的垂直距离。

intro.en: Altitude descends from the Latin word for height and was later borrowed by geography, aviation, and geometry.
intro.cn: altitude 源自拉丁语表示「高度」的词，后来被地理、航空与几何分别借用。

items.en: altus meant 'high, deep', and it also underlies alto and altimeter.
items.cn: altus 意为「高的、深的」，也是 alto 与 altimeter 的来源。

items.en: altitudo was the abstract noun for height or depth.
items.cn: altitudo 是表示高度或深度的抽象名词。

items.en: French passed the word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Mapmakers fixed altitude to height above sea level.
items.cn: 地图绘制者把 altitude 固定为高出海平面的高度。

items.en: Flight added the sense of an aircraft's height at a given moment.
items.cn: 航空又增添了飞机在某一时刻的高度的含义。

items.en: Mathematicians used altitude for the perpendicular height of a figure.
items.cn: 数学家用 altitude 指图形的垂直高。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one syllable; the near-meaning group separates height and elevation.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音节；近义组区分高度与海拔。

definition_zh: 完全；总共；总的来说
definition_en: completely, in total, or considering everything
core_image: 一桌人把各自的钱凑在一起数出一个总数
scene: 结账时大家把账单上的项目加起来，发现总共比预想的多了不少。The meal cost two hundred yuan altogether.
sceneCN: 这里 altogether 是「总共」（第 2 个义项：把各部分加起来得到的总额）；句意是这顿饭总共花了两百元。

pos.zh: 副词：完全；总共；总的来说

derivatives.zh: 短语：大家一起，与 altogether 意义不同
副词：一起，是 altogether 的构词成分
副词：完全，是 altogether 的构词成分
形容词：总的，义近 altogether 的总计用法

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: used to emphasise that something is entirely the case, often with a negative
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事完全如此，常用于否定句中减弱语气
senses.example: The idea is not altogether new.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法并不完全新鲜。
senses.why: All supplies the sense of wholeness and together the sense of gathering into one, so altogether can mean wholly, with every part included.
senses.whyCN: all 提供「全部」，together 提供「聚为一体」，所以 altogether 可以表示「整体上完全如此」，每个部分都算在内。

senses.title: In total
senses.definition: when everything is counted and added up
senses.definitionCN: 把所有项目都算进来、加在一起时
senses.example: The meal cost two hundred yuan altogether.
senses.exampleCN: 这顿饭总共花了两百元。
senses.why: The same gathering of parts can be read as a sum, so the word moves from 'wholly' to 'counting everything'.
senses.whyCN: 同样是把各部分聚在一起，也可以读成求和，于是这个词从「完全」转到「把所有都算上」。

senses.title: Considering everything
senses.definition: used to give an overall judgement after weighing various points
senses.definitionCN: 在权衡各方面之后给出总体判断
senses.example: Altogether, it was a successful trip.
senses.exampleCN: 总的来说，这是一次成功的旅行。
senses.why: When the parts are judgements rather than numbers, the sum becomes an overall verdict, which is why the word can open a concluding sentence.
senses.whyCN: 当被汇总的是各种评价而不是数字时，总和就变成总体结论，因此这个词可以开启总结句。

intro.en: Altogether is an old compound of all and together, and its three senses all grow from the idea of gathering everything into one.
intro.cn: altogether 是 all 与 together 的古老复合词，三个义项都从「把一切聚为一个整体」生长出来。

items.en: eall meant 'all, wholly', the source of modern all.
items.cn: eall 意为「全部、完全」，是现代 all 的来源。

items.en: togædere meant 'in a group, gathered together'.
items.cn: togædere 意为「聚在一起」。

items.en: The phrase meant 'all gathered in one place', first used of people.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「全部聚在一处」，最初用于人。

items.en: The parts fused into one word, which then took on the sense 'wholly'.
items.cn: 两部分合并为一词，随后获得「完全」的含义。

items.en: The counting sense 'in total' and the concluding sense 'on the whole' developed from the same root.
items.cn: 「总共」的计算义与「总的来说」的总结义都从同一词根发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the fused word from the phrase; the near-meaning group shows other summing adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组区分合写词与短语；近义组列出其他表示汇总的副词。

entries.definition: everyone in one group or at one time

normalIntro.en: All plus together: everything gathered into one whole.
normalIntro.cn: all 加 together：所有东西聚成一个整体。

normal.en: Two words all together mean a group in one place.
normal.cn: 分开写的 all together 指一群人待在一起。

normal.en: One word altogether means wholly or in total.
normal.cn: 合写的 altogether 指完全或总共。

normal.en: Not altogether means not entirely.
normal.cn: not altogether 就是并不完全。

normal.en: Altogether can open a conclusion.
normal.cn: altogether 可以引出总结。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: al-to-GE-ther.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：al-to-GE-ther。

abstract.en: Picture coins pushed into one pile.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币被推成一堆。

abstract.en: See a bill with every item added at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象账单底部加出的总数。

abstract.en: Hear a traveller summing up a whole trip.
abstract.cn: 听旅行者给整趟行程下结论。

examples.en: The repairs will cost about five thousand yuan altogether.
examples.cn: 维修总共要花大约五千元。

examples.en: The two designs are altogether different in spirit.
examples.cn: 这两个设计在气质上完全不同。

examples.en: Altogether, the team handled the crisis well.
examples.cn: 总的来说，团队应对这场危机应对得不错。

dict_mnemonic.text: all（全部）加 together（聚在一起）：全部拢成一体，就是完全、总共。

root: 源自古英语 eal togædere「全部聚在一处」，中古英语合并为 altogether，先得「完全」义，再由「把所有部分合起来」发展出「总共」与「总的来说」。

sensesIntro.en: Gathering everything gives three readings: wholly, as a sum, and as an overall verdict.
sensesIntro.cn: 把所有部分聚起来可读出三层意思：完全、总计、总体评价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate coins pushed into one pile.
core.cn: 核心意象：零散硬币被推成一堆。

branches.en: a bill added up at the bottom

branches.cn: 整体判断为成功的旅行

intro.cn: 这是日耳曼复合词，拼写很关键：合写与分写意义不同。

definition_zh: 铝；铝材
definition_en: a light silvery metal that does not rust easily, used for cans, foil, and aircraft parts
core_image: 一卷银亮的铝箔在厨房台面上展开
scene: 厨房里，她把剩菜用铝箔包好，放进冰箱。She wrapped the leftovers in aluminium foil.
sceneCN: 这里 aluminium 是「铝」（第 1 个义项：一种轻而耐锈的银白色金属）；句意是她用铝箔把剩菜包好。

senses.title: The metal element
senses.definition: the chemical element of atomic number thirteen, a light silvery metal that resists corrosion
senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为十三的化学元素，是轻质银白色且耐腐蚀的金属
senses.example: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite by electrolysis.
senses.exampleCN: 铝通过电解从铝土矿中提炼出来。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin alumen, 'alum', the mineral from which the metal was first isolated, so the word begins as a chemical label.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自拉丁语 alumen「明矾」，即最早分离出该金属的矿物，所以这个词起初是化学名称。

senses.title: The metal as a material
senses.definition: the metal considered as an everyday manufacturing material, as in foil, cans, and frames
senses.definitionCN: 把这种金属当作日常制造材料来用，如铝箔、铝罐与框架
senses.example: The window frames are made of aluminium, not steel.
senses.exampleCN: 窗框是铝制的，不是钢的。
senses.why: Because the metal is light and does not rust, industry talks about aluminium as a material to be shaped, which is why it appears in foil, cans, and aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种金属轻且不生锈，工业界把它当作可加工的材料来谈，因此它出现在铝箔、铝罐与飞机部件中。

intro.en: Aluminium is a modern scientific name built on the Latin word for alum.
intro.cn: aluminium 是建立在拉丁语「明矾」一词上的现代科学名称。

items.en: alumen meant 'alum', the mineral salt used in dyeing and medicine.
items.cn: alumen 意为「明矾」，是用于染色与医药的矿物盐。

items.en: English kept alum for the mineral, the source of the metal's name.
items.cn: 英语以 alum 保留了这个矿物名，它正是金属名称的来源。

items.en: Humphry Davy proposed aluminum for the newly isolated metal.
items.cn: 汉弗莱·戴维在 1808 年为新分离出的金属提出 aluminum 这一名称。

items.en: Writers adopted aluminium to match other elements ending in -ium.
items.cn: 人们采用 aluminium，以与其他以 -ium 结尾的元素名一致。

items.en: American English kept Davy's aluminum, while British English kept aluminium.
items.cn: 美式英语沿用戴维的 aluminum，英式英语则用 aluminium。

note.en: The look-alike group covers the spellings and the ore; the near-meaning group places it among metals.
note.cn: 形近组涵盖拼写与矿石；近义组把它放进金属类别。

entries.definition: the American name for the same metal
a mineral salt used in dyeing
aluminium oxide, the white powder from which the metal is refined
entries.definitionCN: 氧化铝，提炼金属用的白色粉末

entries.definition: a hard shiny material that conducts heat and electricity
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬有光泽、能导热导电的材料

entries.definition: a metal mixed with another element
entries.definitionCN: 与其他元素混合的金属

entries.definition: the ore from which aluminium is extracted

normalIntro.en: Aluminium carries the Latin word for alum inside it.
normalIntro.cn: aluminium 里藏着拉丁语的「明矾」一词。

normal.en: Alum plus -inium: the metal from alum.
normal.cn: alum 加 -inium：从明矾来的金属。

normal.en: British aluminium, American aluminum.
normal.cn: 英式写 aluminium，美式写 aluminum。

normal.en: Aluminium foil is the everyday meeting point.
normal.cn: 铝箔是这个词最常见的日常场景。

normal.en: It is light, so it flies: aircraft use aluminium alloys.
normal.cn: 它很轻，所以能飞：飞机构件用铝合金。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: al-u-MIN-i-um.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：al-u-MIN-i-um。

abstract.en: Picture a roll of silver foil unrolling.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷银色铝箔展开。

abstract.en: See a row of drink cans on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象货架上一排饮料罐。

abstract.en: Imagine a light bicycle frame lifted with one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象单手提起的轻质车架。

examples.en: Aluminium is lighter than steel and does not rust.
examples.cn: 铝比钢轻，而且不会生锈。

examples.en: She covered the tray with aluminium foil before baking.
examples.cn: 烘烤前她用铝箔盖住了烤盘。

examples.en: The factory recycles aluminium cans collected from the city.
examples.cn: 这家工厂回收从城里收集来的铝罐。

dict_mnemonic.text: alum（明矾）加 -inium：从明矾里炼出的银白金属，就是铝。

root: 源自拉丁语 alumen「明矾」，英语作 alum；1808 年戴维为新分离的金属造出 aluminum，1812 年又出现 aluminium，以与多数以 -ium 结尾的元素名统一，形成英美两种拼写并存的局面。

sensesIntro.en: The same metal is named twice over: as a chemical element and as a material of industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种金属有两个侧面：化学元素与工业材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a roll of silver foil catching the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷反射光线的银色铝箔。

branches.en: its place in the periodic table
branches.cn: 它在元素周期表中的位置

intro.en: A scientific name with a Latin base and a family of related technical words.
intro.cn: 这是带拉丁词基的科学名称，周围有一族技术词汇。

latinIntro.en: The base alumen is Latin, and the suffix follows the pattern of element names.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 alumen 属拉丁语，后缀沿用元素命名的模式。

definition_zh: 总是；一直；永远；（与进行时连用）老是
definition_en: at every time, for all time, or repeatedly in a way that annoys
core_image: 门口鞋柜上永远摆着同一把旧伞
scene: 每次出门前，奶奶都会检查一遍门窗，从来没有忘过。My grandmother always checks the windows before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里 always 是「总是」（第 1 个义项：每一次都如此）；句意是奶奶出门前总会检查窗户。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：全部的，是 always 的构词成分
名词：路；方式，是 always 的构词成分
副词：永远，义近 always 的永恒义

senses.title: On every occasion
senses.definition: every time a particular situation occurs, without exception
senses.definitionCN: 每当某种情形成立时都如此，没有例外
senses.example: My grandmother always checks the windows before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 我奶奶出门前总会检查窗户。
senses.why: The word began as all the way, meaning the whole course or every time along it, so always marks a habit that holds on every occasion.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是 all the way，意为「整条路、每一次沿途」，所以 always 标记的是在每一次场合都成立的习性。

senses.title: For all time
senses.definition: at all times, forever, or throughout a long period without ending
senses.definitionCN: 在所有时间、永远，或在一段长久时期内始终如此
senses.example: I will always remember that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 我会永远记得那个夏天。
senses.why: If the whole way is unending, the word can stretch from repeated occasions to all time, which is why it appears in promises and memories.
senses.whyCN: 如果这条「整条路」没有尽头，这个词就能从反复的场合延伸到所有时间，因此常出现在承诺与回忆里。

senses.title: Repeatedly, with annoyance
senses.definition: used with a progressive verb to complain that someone keeps doing something
senses.definitionCN: 与进行时连用，抱怨某人一再做某事
senses.example: He is always losing his keys.
senses.exampleCN: 他老是丢钥匙。
senses.why: When always meets the progressive, the repetition becomes a running sore rather than a neutral habit, so the same word turns into a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 当 always 与进行时相遇，重复就变成持续的烦恼而不是中性的习惯，同一个词因此带上了抱怨口气。

intro.en: Always began as a phrase meaning 'all the way', and the road inside it still explains its sense of every occasion.
intro.cn: always 最初是意为「整条路」的短语，其中的「路」仍解释着它「每一次」的含义。

items.en: eall meant 'all, the whole', the source of modern all.
items.cn: eall 意为「全部、整个」，是现代 all 的来源。

items.en: weg meant 'road, way', the ancestor of way.
items.cn: weg 意为「路、方式」，是 way 的前身。

items.en: The phrase meant 'all the way, the whole distance', and it could describe time as well as space.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「整条路、全程」，既可指空间也可指时间。

items.en: The phrase became alway, then always with a final -s copied from adverbs such as towards.
items.cn: 短语先变为 alway，再仿照 towards 等副词加上词尾 -s 成为 always。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the habitual sense and the timeless sense, and adds the complaining progressive use.
items.cn: 现代英语既保留习惯义与永恒义，又增加了带抱怨口气的进行时用法。

note.en: The look-alike group separates always from all ways; the near-meaning group grades frequency and duration.
note.cn: 形近组区分 always 与 all ways；近义组按频率与持续时间分级。

entries.definition: in most cases but not every time

normalIntro.en: All the way, every time: always keeps the road inside it.
normalIntro.cn: 整条路、每一次：always 里仍藏着「路」。

normal.en: All plus way plus -s: the whole road.
normal.cn: all 加 way 再加 -s：整条路。

normal.en: All ways with two words means every method.
normal.cn: 分开写的 all ways 指所有方法。

normal.en: Always usually sits before the main verb.
normal.cn: always 通常放在主要动词之前。

normal.en: Always with -ing sounds like a complaint.
normal.cn: always 配进行时常带抱怨语气。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AL-ways.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AL-ways。

abstract.en: Picture the same old umbrella by the door.
abstract.cn: 想象门口那把一直放着的旧伞。

abstract.en: See a promise written to last forever.
abstract.cn: 想象一句要永远兑现的承诺。

abstract.en: Hear a sigh about lost keys again.
abstract.cn: 听到又丢钥匙时的那声叹气。

examples.en: She always arrives ten minutes early.
examples.cn: 她总是提前十分钟到。

examples.en: I will always be grateful for your help.
examples.cn: 我会永远感激你的帮助。

examples.en: The children are always leaving their toys on the stairs.
examples.cn: 孩子们老是把玩具丢在楼梯上。

dict_mnemonic.text: all（整条）加 way（路）：整条路都如此，就是「总是、一直」。

root: 源自古英语短语 ealne weg「整条路、全程」，中古英语作 alway，后仿 towards 等词加 -s 成 always；由「每一次沿途」引申出「总是」，再引申出「永远」与抱怨性的反复。

sensesIntro.en: A whole road without exception yields habit, eternity, and irritated repetition.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条毫无例外的整路，生出习惯、永恒与恼人的反复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old umbrella that is always by the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：永远放在门口的那把旧伞。

branches.en: a promise that will not fade

intro.en: A worn-down Germanic phrase, now felt as one adverb.
intro.cn: 这是磨合成一体的日耳曼短语，如今被当作单个副词。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Germanic, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 成分属于日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 业余爱好者；业余的；外行的
definition_en: a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure rather than for money, or someone lacking professional skill
core_image: 周末公园里，一群爱好者扛着相机拍鸟
scene: 社区球场上，一群下班后赶来的球员换上球衣，没有一个人拿报酬。The tournament is open to amateur players only.
sceneCN: 这里 amateur 是「业余的」（第 2 个义项：不以该项活动为职业、不取报酬）；句意是这项赛事只对业余选手开放。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：业余水平的；不够专业的
名词：业余主义；业余身份
形容词：爱情的，与 amateur 同源于拉丁语「爱」

senses.title: One who does it for love
senses.definition: a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure rather than as a job
senses.definitionCN: 出于兴趣而非职业参加某项活动的人
senses.example: He is a keen amateur photographer on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 他周末是个热心的业余摄影爱好者。
senses.why: The word goes back to Latin amator, 'lover', so an amateur is literally someone who does the activity for the love of it rather than for pay.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可追溯到拉丁语 amator「爱者」，所以 amateur 字面上就是因热爱而做某件事的人，而不是为报酬而做。

senses.title: Not professional
senses.definition: describing sport, art, or work done outside a profession and usually without payment
senses.definitionCN: 形容在职业体系之外进行、通常没有报酬的运动、艺术或工作
senses.example: The tournament is open to amateur players only.
senses.exampleCN: 这项赛事只对业余选手开放。
senses.why: Once amateur names the person, it can describe the whole level of activity, setting it against the paid professional circuit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 amateur 能指人，它也能形容整个活动层级，与有报酬的职业圈相对。

senses.title: A clumsy non-expert
senses.definition: a disapproving word for someone whose work shows lack of professional skill
senses.definitionCN: 带贬义，指工作显出缺乏专业训练的人
senses.example: The repairs were done by amateurs and soon fell apart.
senses.exampleCN: 这些维修是外行做的，很快就散架了。
senses.why: Because love without training can look clumsy, the word acquired a sneer: an amateur is not merely unpaid but unskilled.
senses.whyCN: 因为只有热爱而缺乏训练往往显得笨拙，这个词便带上讥讽：amateur 不只是没有报酬，还是技艺不精。

intro.en: Amateur is a love word: it descends from the Latin verb 'to love'.
intro.cn: amateur 是个与「爱」有关的词，源自拉丁语动词「爱」。

items.en: amare meant 'to love', the source of amatory and of amateur.
items.cn: amare 意为「爱」，是 amatory 与 amateur 的来源。

items.en: amator meant 'lover, one who loves', without any hint of incompetence.
items.cn: amator 意为「爱者、热爱者」，丝毫没有不专业的意思。

items.en: French amateur named someone who cultivates an art or sport for pleasure.
items.cn: 法语 amateur 指为兴趣而从事艺术或运动的人。

items.en: English adopted the word for the growing world of clubs, sports, and hobbies.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入该词，用于兴起的俱乐部、运动与爱好圈子。

items.en: The disapproving sense 'unskilled' developed alongside the neutral one, so context decides the tone.
items.cn: 贬义的「不熟练」与中性的「业余」并行发展，语气由语境决定。

note.en: The look-alike group grows from the same root; the near-meaning group contrasts levels of skill and pay.
note.cn: 形近组同出一源；近义组对比技艺与报酬的层级。

entries.definition: the belief that sport should stay unpaid

paid and trained in a field

normalIntro.en: Amateur comes from love, not from lack.
normalIntro.cn: amateur 来自「爱」，而不是来自「缺少」。

normal.en: Latin amare means to love.
normal.cn: 拉丁 amare 意为爱。

normal.en: An amateur does it for love, a professional for pay.
normal.cn: 业余者为热爱而做，职业者为报酬而做。

normal.en: Amateurish is the adjective of disapproval.
normal.cn: amateurish 是带贬义的形容词。

normal.en: Amateur dramatics is a common British phrase.
normal.cn: amateur dramatics 是常见的英式说法。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AM-a-teur.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AM-a-teur。

abstract.en: Picture a weekend photographer with a heavy bag.
abstract.cn: 想象周末背着沉重器材的摄影爱好者。

abstract.en: See a local team playing for fun.
abstract.cn: 想象本地队伍为乐趣而踢球。

abstract.en: Hear a critic calling the work amateurish.
abstract.cn: 听到评论者说这作品像外行做的。

examples.en: She plays tennis as an amateur, but she trains every morning.
examples.cn: 她以业余身份打网球，但每天早上都训练。

examples.en: The exhibition gives amateur artists a chance to show their work.
examples.cn: 这个展览给业余艺术家展示作品的机会。

examples.en: The wiring looked amateur and had to be redone.
examples.cn: 布线看起来很不专业，只好重做。

dict_mnemonic.text: amateur 与 amare「爱」同源：因热爱而做，不为报酬，就是业余。

root: 源自拉丁语 amare「爱」的派生词 amator「爱者」，经法语 amateur 于十八世纪进入英语，本指因热爱而从事某项活动的人，后发展出「非职业」与贬义的「外行」两层用法。

sensesIntro.en: Love of the activity yields three readings: the enthusiast, the unpaid level, and the unskilled outsider.
sensesIntro.cn: 对活动的热爱生出三种读法：爱好者、非职业层级、技艺不精的外行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weekend photographer who shoots for joy.
core.cn: 核心意象：为快乐而拍照的周末摄影者。

intro.en: A Latin love root with a small family of English derivatives.
intro.cn: 这是拉丁语「爱」的词根，带出一小族英语派生词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb amare and the noun amator are the source of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 amare 与名词 amator 是这一词族的来源。

items.meaning: one who does something for love

definition_zh: 使惊奇；使惊叹
definition_en: to surprise someone very much, often with something impressive or hard to believe
core_image: 观众仰头看着魔术师让整架钢琴凭空消失
scene: 魔术师把硬币从空中变出来，台下的孩子张大了嘴。The trick amazed the whole audience.
sceneCN: 这里 amaze 是「使惊奇」（第 1 个义项：因出乎意料或难以置信而使人震惊）；句意是这个魔术让全场观众惊叹。

senses.title: To surprise greatly
senses.definition: to surprise someone strongly with something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 用出乎意料的事让人受到强烈震动
senses.example: The trick amazed the whole audience.
senses.exampleCN: 这个魔术让全场观众惊叹。
senses.why: The word began as a verb meaning to confuse or stupefy, so the core of amaze is not mild surprise but being mentally knocked off balance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初意为「使困惑、使发懵」，所以 amaze 的核心不是轻微的意外，而是让人一时失去思考的平衡。

senses.title: To fill with wonder
senses.definition: to impress someone deeply with something beautiful, vast, or skilful
senses.definitionCN: 以美丽、宏大或技艺高超之物深深打动某人
senses.example: Her courage amazed everyone who knew her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的勇气让认识她的人都由衷赞叹。
senses.why: When the cause is admirable rather than merely unexpected, the same shock turns into wonder, which is why amazing often carries praise.
senses.whyCN: 当引起震动的对象不只是意外，而且令人钦佩时，同样的冲击就转为赞叹，所以 amazing 常带褒义。

intro.en: Amaze began as a word for mental confusion, and only later settled into wonder.
intro.cn: amaze 最初表示头脑混乱，后来才固定为惊叹。

items.en: amasian meant 'to confuse, to stupefy', formed with the prefix a- on a base related to maze.
items.cn: amasian 意为「使困惑、使发懵」，由前缀 a- 加与 maze 相关的词基构成。

items.en: The verb still meant 'to bewilder', with fear and confusion in the foreground.
items.cn: 这个动词仍意为「使迷惑」，恐惧与混乱是其重点。

items.en: Amaze shifted towards 'to overwhelm with wonder', losing most of its old sense of panic.
items.cn: 十六世纪 amaze 转向「以惊奇压倒人」，旧有的惊慌义大体消失。

items.en: Amazement and amazing grew alongside, and amazing later became a general adjective of praise.
items.cn: amazement 与 amazing 随之发展，amazing 后来成为泛用的褒义形容词。

items.en: Modern amaze is a strong but usually positive word, close to astonish but warmer.
items.cn: 现代 amaze 语气强烈但通常偏正面，接近 astonish 却更带温度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the maze base; the near-meaning group grades the strength of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组共享 maze 词基；近义组按惊讶强度分级。

normalIntro.en: Amaze is a-maze: the mind is put into a maze.
normalIntro.cn: amaze 可拆成 a 加 maze：把人的脑子放进迷宫。

normal.en: A maze bewilders, and amaze once meant bewilder.
normal.cn: 迷宫使人迷失，amaze 曾经就意为使人迷失。

normal.en: Amazing is the adjective of praise.
normal.cn: amazing 是表示赞叹的形容词。

normal.en: Be amazed at or by, not with.
normal.cn: 搭配是 be amazed at 或 by，不用 with。

normal.en: Never cease to amaze is a fixed phrase.
normal.cn: never cease to amaze 是固定说法。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-MAZE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-MAZE。

abstract.en: Picture a vanishing piano on stage.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上凭空消失的钢琴。

abstract.en: See a child's mouth open at a magic trick.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子看魔术时张大的嘴。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd silent for a second, then cheering.
abstract.cn: 想象全场静了一秒，随后欢呼。

examples.en: The speed of the recovery amazed the doctors.
examples.cn: 恢复的速度让医生们惊叹。

examples.en: We were amazed at how quiet the city felt at dawn.
examples.cn: 黎明时城市的安静让我们惊讶。

examples.en: Her ability to remember names never ceases to amaze me.
examples.cn: 她记名字的本领总让我惊叹。

dict_mnemonic.text: a 加 maze（迷宫）：把人带进迷宫，脑子转不出来，就是「使惊奇」。

root: 源自古英语 amasian「使困惑、使发懵」，由前缀 a- 加与 maze「迷宫」相关的词基构成；十六世纪起转向「以惊奇压倒人」，并派生出 amazement、amazing 等词。

sensesIntro.en: A shock to the mind can be mere surprise or admiring wonder, and the word covers both.
sensesIntro.cn: 对头脑的冲击可以是单纯的意外，也可以是钦佩的赞叹，这个词两者都包。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind lost in a maze of surprise.
core.cn: 核心意象：思绪被困在惊讶的迷宫里。

branches.en: a view that silences a crowd
a memory for names that never fails

intro.en: An Old English verb with the a- prefix and a maze-related base.
intro.cn: 这是带 a- 前缀、词基与迷宫有关的古英语动词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 大使；使节；（品牌或事业的）代表
definition_en: the senior diplomat sent by a country to another, or a person who represents a brand or cause
core_image: 大使馆门前，一位身着正装的人递交国书
scene: 新任大使在总统府递交国书，随后与当地官员握手寒暄。The new ambassador presented her credentials at the palace.
sceneCN: 这里 ambassador 是「大使」（第 1 个义项：一国派往另一国的最高外交代表）；句意是新任大使在总统府递交国书。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：大使的；大使级的
名词：女大使；大使夫人，旧用法
名词：大使馆；使馆全体人员

senses.title: A country's top diplomat
senses.definition: the senior official who represents one country's government in another country
senses.definitionCN: 一国政府派驻另一国的最高级别代表
senses.example: The new ambassador presented her credentials at the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 新任大使在总统府递交了国书。
senses.why: The word goes back to a medieval term for a mission or service, so an ambassador is the person sent to carry out that mission abroad.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可追溯到中世纪表示「使命、差事」的词，所以大使就是被派往国外执行这项使命的人。

senses.title: A representative of a brand or cause
senses.definition: a well-known person who publicly represents a company, charity, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 公开代表某公司、慈善机构或理念的知名人物
senses.example: The retired player became an ambassador for the children's charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退役球员成了该儿童慈善机构的代言人。
senses.why: A diplomat speaks for a country, and modern marketing borrowed that role: the brand ambassador speaks for a brand in public.
senses.whyCN: 外交官代表国家发声，现代营销借用了这个角色：品牌代言人在公众场合代表品牌。

intro.en: Ambassador came into English from French, and its deeper origin is a word for service or mission.
intro.cn: ambassador 经法语进入英语，更早的来源是表示「服务、使命」的词。

items.en: A Celtic word ambactus meant 'servant, retainer', and it passed into Latin.
items.cn: 凯尔特语 ambactus 意为「仆人、随从」，并传入拉丁语。

items.en: ambactia meant 'service, mission', the duty a retainer carried out.
items.cn: ambactia 意为「服务、使命」，即随从承担的任务。

items.en: French named the person who carried out such a mission, and English borrowed the form.
items.cn: 法语用 ambassadeur 指执行这类使命的人，英语借用了这一形式。

items.en: English ambassador first meant a messenger or representative of a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 ambassador 最初指君主的信使或代表。

items.en: The diplomatic sense became fixed, and the twentieth century added the brand ambassador.
items.cn: 外交义固定下来，二十世纪又增添了品牌代言人的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the embassy family; the near-meaning group ranks diplomatic roles.
note.cn: 形近组是使馆词族；近义组按外交职级排列。

entries.definition: the office and staff of an ambassador
a female ambassador or ambassador's wife
a messenger or representative sent on a special mission
an official who represents a country abroad
an official who protects citizens in a foreign city

normalIntro.en: An ambassador is the person sent on the mission.
normalIntro.cn: ambassador 就是被派去执行使命的人。

normal.en: Embassy is the building, ambassador is the person.
normal.cn: embassy 是使馆建筑，ambassador 是人。

normal.en: Ambassador to a country, not ambassador in.
normal.cn: 说 ambassador to 某国，而不是 ambassador in。

normal.en: Brand ambassador borrows the diplomatic role.
normal.cn: brand ambassador 借用了外交角色。

normal.en: Recall an ambassador when relations break down.
normal.cn: 关系破裂时会把大使召回。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节。

abstract.en: Picture credentials handed over in a palace.
abstract.cn: 想象在总统府递交国书。

abstract.en: See a flag and a formal handshake.
abstract.cn: 想象国旗与正式握手。

abstract.en: Imagine a famous face speaking for a charity.
abstract.cn: 想象名人替慈善机构发声。

examples.en: She was appointed ambassador to Norway last year.
examples.cn: 她去年被任命为驻挪威大使。

examples.en: The ambassador met the foreign minister for talks.
examples.cn: 大使会晤外长进行会谈。

examples.en: The singer acts as an ambassador for a wildlife charity.
examples.cn: 这位歌手担任一家野生动物慈善机构的代言人。

dict_mnemonic.text: ambassador 与 embassy 同族：使馆里那位最高代表，就是大使。

root: 源自凯尔特语 ambactus「仆人、随从」，经中世纪拉丁语 ambactia「服务、使命」与古法语 ambassadeur 于十四世纪进入英语，先指君主的信使，后固定为驻外最高外交代表，现代又引申出品牌代言人。

sensesIntro.en: One role, the mission's representative, now covers both diplomacy and public advocacy.
sensesIntro.cn: 「使命的代表」这一角色，如今同时覆盖外交与公共代言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: credentials handed over at a palace.
core.cn: 核心意象：在总统府递交国书。

branches.cn: 巡回宣传的品牌代言人

intro.en: A Romance word with a compact family around embassy and ambassador.
intro.cn: 这是罗曼语词，围绕 embassy 与 ambassador 有一小族词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin ambactia is the bridge between the Celtic root and the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 ambactia 是凯尔特词根与法语词之间的桥梁。

definition_zh: 雄心；抱负；野心；志向
definition_en: a strong desire to achieve something, or the particular goal that desire is aimed at
core_image: 登山者抬头望着远处的顶峰，脚下还有很长的路
scene: 她在日记里写下十年后的目标：开一家自己的诊所。Her ambition is to run her own clinic one day.
sceneCN: 这里 ambition 是「志向；抱负」（第 2 个义项：想要达成的具体目标）；句意是她的志向是有朝一日经营自己的诊所。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有雄心的；野心勃勃的
名词：范围；界限，与 ambition 同为拉丁词根

senses.title: The drive to succeed
senses.definition: a strong inner desire to achieve success, power, or a high position
senses.definitionCN: 内心强烈地想要取得成就、权力或高位的愿望
senses.example: Her ambition drove her to study late into the night.
senses.exampleCN: 她的雄心驱使她学习到深夜。
senses.why: The Latin root meant 'a going around', the walk a candidate made to gather votes, so ambition began as the restless movement of someone seeking office.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「四处走动」，即候选人拉票时的奔走，所以 ambition 最初就是谋求职位者那种停不下来的行动。

senses.title: A specific goal
senses.definition: the particular thing a person strongly wants to achieve in life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人一生中强烈想要达成的具体事情
senses.example: Her ambition is to run her own clinic one day.
senses.exampleCN: 她的志向是有朝一日经营自己的诊所。
senses.why: Once the drive has an object, the word can name that object directly, which is why ambition can be followed by a to-infinitive or a noun.
senses.whyCN: 当这股冲劲有了对象，这个词就可以直接指那个对象，因此 ambition 后可接不定式或名词。

intro.en: Ambition began as a word for political canvassing, and it still carries a whiff of the campaign trail.
intro.cn: ambition 最初指政治拉票，至今仍带着竞选路上的气味。

items.en: ambire meant 'to go around', formed from amb- 'about' and ire 'to go'.
items.cn: ambire 意为「四处走动」，由 amb-「周围」与 ire「走」构成。

items.en: ambitio named the round of visits a candidate made to win votes.
items.cn: ambitio 指候选人为了拉票而进行的一轮走访。

items.en: Roman writers used ambitio for self-seeking and vote-chasing, giving the word its darker edge.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 ambitio 指钻营与拉票，赋予这个词阴暗的一面。

items.en: French softened the word into a general desire for honour or success.
items.cn: 法语把这个词软化为对荣誉或成功的普遍渴望。

items.en: English keeps both faces: ambition as admirable drive and ambition as self-serving greed.
items.cn: 英语保留了两副面孔：令人钦佩的进取心，以及自私的贪欲。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin base; the near-meaning group grades desire and goals.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词基；近义组区分渴望与目标。

entries.definition: having a strong desire to succeed
the scope or limits of something
a hope or aim of achieving something

normalIntro.en: Ambition is a going around: the candidate walking for votes.
normalIntro.cn: ambition 是「四处奔走」：候选人为了选票到处走。

normal.en: Latin ambire means to go around.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ambire 意为四处走动。

normal.en: Ambition can be noble drive or selfish greed.
normal.cn: ambition 既可以是可敬的进取，也可以是自私的贪欲。

normal.en: The adjective is ambitious, not ambitioned.
normal.cn: 形容词是 ambitious，不是 ambitioned。

normal.en: Achieve or fulfil an ambition.
normal.cn: 搭配是 achieve 或 fulfil an ambition。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: am-BI-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：am-BI-tion。

abstract.en: Picture a climber looking at a distant summit.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者望着远处的顶峰。

abstract.en: See a candidate walking from door to door.
abstract.cn: 想象候选人挨家挨户走访。

abstract.en: Imagine a notebook page with a ten-year goal.
abstract.cn: 想象日记本上写下十年后的目标。

examples.en: His ambition is to become a pilot.
examples.cn: 他的志向是成为一名飞行员。

examples.en: She has the ambition and the discipline to finish the course.
examples.cn: 她有完成这门课程的雄心和自律。

examples.en: The plan was criticized as pure political ambition.
examples.cn: 这个计划被批评为纯粹的政治野心。

dict_mnemonic.text: ambi 意为「周围」，ire 意为「走」：为选票四处奔走，就是野心与抱负。

root: 源自拉丁语 ambire「四处走动」，其名词 ambitio 指候选人拉票时的奔走，罗马作家用它表示钻营；经法语 ambition 进入英语后，兼有可敬的进取心与自私的野心两面。

sensesIntro.en: The word names both the restless drive and the object it aims at.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指那股停不下来的冲劲，也指它瞄准的目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a climber eyeing a summit far above.
core.cn: 核心意象：登山者望着高处的顶峰。

branches.en: a wish to become a pilot
a lifelong dream of a clinic

intro.en: A Latin verb of motion turned into a noun of desire, with a small English family.
intro.cn: 这是拉丁语运动动词转成的欲望名词，英语中有一小族派生词。

latinIntro.en: The verb ambire and the noun ambitio supply the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 动词 ambire 与名词 ambitio 提供历史词基。

definition_zh: 救护车；急救运输服务
definition_en: a vehicle that takes sick or injured people to hospital, or the emergency service that runs it
core_image: 闪着蓝灯的白色车辆穿过拥堵的街道
scene: 有人倒在路边，路人立刻拨打电话叫救护车。Someone called an ambulance as soon as the man collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里 ambulance 是「救护车」（第 1 个义项：运送伤病者去医院的车辆）；句意是那人一倒下，就有人叫了救护车。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：可走动的；门诊的，与 ambulance 同源
名词：救护车司机；急救员
动词：漫步，与 ambulance 同源于拉丁语「走」

senses.title: The emergency vehicle
senses.definition: a vehicle equipped to carry sick or injured people to hospital, often with flashing lights and a siren
senses.definitionCN: 装有急救设备、把伤病者送往医院的车辆，常带闪灯与警笛
senses.example: Someone called an ambulance as soon as the man collapsed.
senses.exampleCN: 那人一倒下，就有人叫了救护车。
senses.why: The word began as French hôpital ambulant, a 'walking hospital', and the vehicle inherited that name because treatment could move with the patient.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是法语 hôpital ambulant「行走的医院」，车辆沿用了这个名字，因为治疗可以随病人一起移动。

senses.title: The emergency service
senses.definition: the organised service, staff, and vehicles that respond to medical emergencies
senses.definitionCN: 应对医疗急症的有组织服务、人员与车辆体系
senses.example: The ambulance service in the region is short of staff.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的急救服务人手不足。
senses.why: Once the vehicle became familiar, the same noun could name the whole system that dispatches it, especially in phrases such as ambulance service.
senses.whyCN: 当这种车辆变得常见之后，同一个名词也能指调度它的整套体系，尤其在 ambulance service 这类短语里。

intro.en: Ambulance began as a moving hospital, and the Latin verb inside it simply means 'to walk'.
intro.cn: ambulance 最初指会移动的医院，其中的拉丁动词本义就是「走」。

items.en: ambulare meant 'to walk, to move about', the source of amble and ambulatory.

items.en: French field hospitals were called hôpital ambulant, a hospital that moved with the army.

definition_en: in the middle of a situation, group, or place, especially one full of activity or difficulty

scene: 会场里掌声不断，她走上台接过奖杯，脸上却没太多表情。She accepted the award amid loud applause.
sceneCN: 这里 amid 是「在……之中」（第 1 个义项：某事在另一种情形或氛围当中发生）；句意是她在热烈掌声中接过奖项。

senses.title: In the middle of an event
senses.definition: while something else is happening around the subject, often something noisy, tense, or difficult
senses.definitionCN: 在主语周围正发生另一件事时，常指喧闹、紧张或困难的局面
senses.example: She accepted the award amid loud applause.
senses.exampleCN: 她在热烈掌声中接过奖项。
senses.why: The word is a worn form of on middan, 'in the middle', so amid places an event inside the surrounding circumstances rather than merely near them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 on middan「在中间」的磨损形式，所以 amid 把事件放进周围的情境之内，而不只是在其附近。

senses.title: Surrounded by things
senses.definition: surrounded by physical things or people, used in a slightly literary way
senses.definitionCN: 四周是具体的事物或人，带一点书面色彩
senses.example: The cottage stands amid tall pine trees.
senses.exampleCN: 小屋立在高大的松树之间。
senses.why: The older spatial sense survives in descriptions of landscape, where amid simply means the subject is enclosed by what surrounds it.
senses.whyCN: 较早的空间义保留在景物描写中，此时 amid 只表示主体被周围事物围在中间。

intro.en: Amid is a worn-down Old English phrase meaning 'in the middle'.
intro.cn: amid 是古英语短语「在中间」磨损后的形式。

items.cn: 这一短语意为「在……中间」，既用于地点也用于人群。

items.en: The phrase fused into amidde, and the final -e was later lost.
items.cn: 短语合并为 amidde，词尾 -e 后来脱落。

items.en: Modern amid is mainly literary and often introduces circumstances rather than physical space.
items.cn: 现代 amid 主要用于书面语，常引出情境而不是具体空间。

definition_zh: 在……中间；在……之中；是……之一；在……之间分配
definition_en: surrounded by or included in a group, or shared by the members of a group
core_image: 一群孩子围坐成一圈，其中一个正说着话
scene: 她在新学校里很快交到朋友，午餐时总有人叫她一起坐。She soon felt at home among her new classmates.
sceneCN: 这里 among 是「在……中间」（第 1 个义项：处在一群人之内、被他们围绕）；句意是她很快在新同学中间自在了。

senses.title: In the company of a group
senses.definition: surrounded by people or things that form a group around the subject
senses.definitionCN: 周围是构成一群的人或物，主语处在这群之中
senses.example: She soon felt at home among her new classmates.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快在新同学中间自在了。
senses.why: The word comes from on gemang, 'in the mingling', so among pictures the subject mixed into a group rather than standing outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 on gemang「在混杂之中」，所以 among 描绘的是主语混进一群人里，而不是站在群体之外。

senses.title: One of a set
senses.definition: included as one member of a larger set or category
senses.definitionCN: 作为更大集合或类别中的一员被包括在内
senses.example: The novel is among the best of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是年度最佳之一。
senses.why: If the subject is inside the mingling, it can be counted as one of the members, which gives the 'one of' sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果主语处在混杂之中，它就可以被算作其中一员，于是产生「其中之一」的用法。

senses.title: Shared by the members
senses.definition: used of something divided or shared by three or more people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 指某物由三个或更多的人或群体分配或共享
senses.example: The money was divided among the four villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔钱分给了四个村庄。
senses.why: The same group image serves distribution: what is placed in the middle of a group is then shared out to its members.
senses.whyCN: 同样的群体意象也可用于分配：放在群体中间的东西，随后被分给各个成员。

intro.en: Among began as a phrase about mingling, and its root still survives in mingle.

senses.title: In the middle of a group
senses.definition: surrounded by or in the company of a group, used especially in written or older style
senses.definitionCN: 被一群人围绕或与他们在一起，多用于书面或较旧的文体
senses.example: The writer hoped to grow old amongst friends.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家希望能在朋友中间安度晚年。
senses.why: The -st is an added ending that spread in Middle English, giving a longer, more formal-sounding form of among without changing the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -st 是中古英语扩散开来的附加结尾，使 among 多了一个更长、更正式的形态，词义并未改变。

senses.title: Shared within a group

senses.why: Since amongst is only a longer among, it inherits the distribution sense as well, and the formal tone suits legal or historical writing.
