senses.title: A quantity of something
senses.definition: how much of something there is, especially something that cannot be counted one by one
senses.definitionCN: 某物有多少，尤指无法逐个数清的东西
senses.example: The recipe needs a small amount of salt.
senses.exampleCN: 这道菜需要少量的盐。
senses.why: The verb behind the word meant 'to go up', and a quantity was seen as a total that rises as more is added.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的动词意为「上升」，数量被看作随着增加而不断升高的总数。

senses.title: A sum of money
senses.definition: a particular sum of money, especially one paid or owed
senses.definitionCN: 一笔特定的钱，尤指支付或欠下的款项
senses.example: She paid the full amount without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫无怨言地付了全款。
senses.why: Money is the most common thing that adds up, so the counting sense narrowed into a fixed financial sum.
senses.whyCN: 钱是最常被累加的东西，于是「计数」义收窄为固定的金额。

senses.title: To total or be equivalent
senses.definition: used as a verb with to, meaning to add up to a figure or to be effectively the same as something
senses.definitionCN: 作动词与 to 连用，表示合计达到某数字，或实际上等同于某事
senses.example: The bills amount to twice what we paid last month.
senses.exampleCN: 这些账单合计是我们上月所付的两倍。
senses.why: If a quantity rises as parts are added, the verb can state the final figure, and from there it extends to 'be equivalent to' in meaning.
senses.whyCN: 如果数量随各部分相加而升高，动词就可以说出最终数字，再由此引申为「在意义上等同于」。

intro.en: Amount climbs: it comes from a French verb meaning to go up, and the hill inside it is still visible in mountain.
intro.cn: amount 是「往上走」的词：它来自法语动词「上升」，其中的「山」仍见于 mountain。

items.en: The phrase meant 'to the hill', from mons, 'mountain'.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「向山而去」，来自 mons「山」。

items.en: amont meant 'up, uphill', the base of the verb amonter.
items.cn: amont 意为「向上、往山上」，是动词 amonter 的词基。

items.en: amonter meant 'to go up, to rise', and also 'to add up to a total'.
items.cn: amonter 意为「上升」，也表示「合计达到某数」。

items.en: English took the noun as amount, 'a total, a quantity'.
items.cn: 英语借入名词 amount，意为「总数、数量」。

items.en: The verb amount to now covers both totals and figurative equivalence.
items.cn: 动词短语 amount to 如今既指金额合计，也指抽象的「等同于」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the hill root; the near-meaning group separates quantity words.
note.cn: 形近组共享「山」词根；近义组区分数量词。

normalIntro.en: Amount goes uphill: more parts make a higher total.
normalIntro.cn: amount 是往上走的：部分越多，总数越高。

normal.en: Amount to means add up to or be equivalent to.
normal.cn: amount to 意为合计为或等同于。

normal.en: Use amount for things you cannot count one by one.
normal.cn: 无法逐个数的东西用 amount。

normal.en: Number is for countable things, amount for mass.
normal.cn: number 用于可数事物，amount 用于不可数事物。

normal.en: No amount of apology will fix it.
normal.cn: 再多的道歉也弥补不了。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-MOUNT.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-MOUNT。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt with a growing column of figures.
abstract.cn: 想象收据上一列不断增长的数字。

abstract.en: See a pile of sand rising higher.
abstract.cn: 想象沙堆越堆越高。

abstract.en: Imagine a bill that equals a month's salary.
abstract.cn: 想象一张等于一个月工资的账单。

examples.en: A large amount of water was wasted.
examples.cn: 大量的水被浪费了。

examples.en: The insurance company paid the full amount.
examples.cn: 保险公司支付了全额。

examples.en: His silence amounted to an admission of guilt.
examples.cn: 他的沉默等同于认罪。

dict_mnemonic.text: a 加 mount（山、上升）：数字往山上走，就是数量与总额。

root: 源自拉丁语 ad montem「向山而去」，经古法语 amont「向上」与动词 amonter「上升、合计」进入英语，先作名词表示总数与数量，再作动词 amount to 表示合计或等同于。

sensesIntro.en: A rising total gives a quantity, then a sum of money, then the verb of adding up or amounting to.
sensesIntro.cn: 上升的总数先给出数量，再给出金额，最后给出表示合计与等同的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of figures rising to a total.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列数字升到一个总额。

branches.en: the full amount on a bill
bills amounting to twice last month
branches.cn: 合计为上月两倍的账单

intro.en: A Romance word whose hill root also produced mount and mountain.
intro.cn: 这是罗曼语词，其「山」词根也产生了 mount 与 mountain。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun mons, 'mountain', lies behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 mons「山」是整族词的底层来源。

definition_zh: 使发笑；逗乐；给……提供消遣
definition_en: to make someone laugh or smile, or to keep someone pleasantly occupied
core_image: 候车室里，一个孩子用纸折出小动物逗弟弟笑
scene: 长途车上，邻座的人讲了几个笑话，把整排乘客都逗笑了。The jokes amused the tired passengers.
sceneCN: 这里 amuse 是「逗乐；使发笑」（第 1 个义项：让人笑起来）；句意是这些笑话把疲惫的乘客逗乐了。

pos.zh: 动词：使发笑；逗乐；给……消遣

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有趣的；逗人笑的

senses.title: To make someone laugh
senses.definition: to cause someone to laugh or smile, usually with something funny
senses.definitionCN: 用有趣的东西让人发笑或微笑
senses.example: The jokes amused the tired passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些笑话把疲惫的乘客逗乐了。
senses.why: The word began in French with a sense of distracting or stupefying the mind, and laughter is the gentlest form of that distraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初在法语中意为分散注意、使头脑发懵，而笑声正是这种分神最温和的形式。

senses.title: To keep pleasantly occupied
senses.definition: to give someone something enjoyable to do so that time passes happily
senses.definitionCN: 给某人有趣的事情做，使时间愉快地过去
senses.example: The museum keeps children amused for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆能让孩子们开心地待上几个小时。
senses.why: Amusement need not be laughter; anything that holds attention pleasantly keeps the mind from boredom, which is the older sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 消遣不一定要有笑声；任何能愉快地占据注意力、使心思不落到无聊上的东西都算，这正是这个词较早的含义。

intro.en: Amuse originally meant to distract the mind, not to make it laugh.
intro.cn: amuse 最初指分散心思，而不是让人发笑。

items.en: muser meant 'to stare, to ponder, to waste time', the base of the word.
items.cn: muser 意为「呆看、沉思、消磨时间」，是该词的词基。

items.en: amuser meant 'to deceive, to stupefy, to divert attention'.
items.cn: amuser 意为「欺骗、使发懵、转移注意力」。

items.en: English amuse first meant 'to divert the attention, to occupy'.
items.cn: 英语 amuse 最初意为「转移注意力、使忙碌」。

items.en: The sense narrowed towards pleasant diversion and then to making people laugh.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄为愉快的消遣，随后又指逗人发笑。

items.en: Amusing now usually means funny, while amusement covers both laughter and pastime.
items.cn: 如今 amusing 通常指好笑，而 amusement 既指笑也指消遣。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the muse base; the near-meaning group grades entertainment.
note.cn: 形近组共享 muse 词基；近义组按娱乐方式分级。

normalIntro.en: Amuse is a-muse: to lead the mind away from boredom.
normalIntro.cn: amuse 可看作 a 加 muse：把心思从无聊中引开。

normal.en: Muse means to ponder; amuse first meant to distract.
normal.cn: muse 意为沉思，amuse 最初意为分散注意。

normal.en: Amusing is the adjective for something funny.
normal.cn: amusing 是形容某物好笑的形容词。

normal.en: Be amused by, not amused from.
normal.cn: 搭配是 be amused by，不用 from。

normal.en: An amusement park is a place of pastime.
normal.cn: amusement park 是消遣之地。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-MUSE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-MUSE。

abstract.en: Picture a paper animal folded on a bus.
abstract.cn: 想象在公交车上折出的纸动物。

abstract.en: See a row of passengers smiling at a joke.
abstract.cn: 想象一排乘客被笑话逗笑。

abstract.en: Imagine a child busy for hours in a museum.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子在博物馆里玩上几个小时。

examples.en: The clown amused the children for an hour.
examples.cn: 小丑逗孩子们开心了一个小时。

examples.en: I was amused by his imitation of the teacher.
examples.cn: 他模仿老师的样子把我逗乐了。

examples.en: She amused herself by reading old letters.
examples.cn: 她读旧信来消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: a 加 muse（沉思）：把沉思的人拉出来，就是逗乐、消遣。

root: 源自古法语 amuser「欺骗、使发懵、转移注意」，其词基 muser 意为呆看、沉思；十五世纪进入英语时意为转移注意力，十七世纪渐指愉快的消遣，现代更常指逗人发笑。

sensesIntro.en: Diverting the mind yields two uses: provoking laughter and filling time pleasantly.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把心思引开」生出两种用法：引人发笑，以及愉快地打发时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded paper animal making a child smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：折纸小动物逗笑孩子。

branches.en: jokes on a long bus ride

branches.cn: 让孩子有事可做的博物馆

branches.en: reading old letters to pass time

intro.en: A French verb with a compact English family around amusement.
intro.cn: 这是法语动词，英语中围绕 amusement 有一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The word is French rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自法语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 分析；分解；对……作精神分析
definition_en: to examine something in detail by breaking it into parts, or to treat someone with psychoanalysis
core_image: 把一台旧钟拆开，零件一件件摆在桌上查看
scene: 实验室里，技术员把水样分成几份，逐一检测其中的成分。The lab analysed the water samples for traces of lead.
sceneCN: 这里 analyse 是「分析；化验」（第 2 个义项：把物质分解开来检测成分）；句意是实验室检测水样中是否含铅。

pos.zh: 动词：分析；分解；作精神分析

senses.title: To examine in detail
senses.definition: to study something closely by separating it into its parts in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物拆成若干部分仔细研究，以求理解
senses.example: Researchers analysed the data from ten thousand households.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员分析了一万个家庭的数据。
senses.why: The Greek verb behind the word meant 'to loosen up', so to analyse is to loosen a whole into its parts until the structure shows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的希腊动词意为「解开」，所以 analyse 就是把整体拆松成部分，直到结构显露出来。

senses.title: To test a substance
senses.definition: to break a substance down chemically in order to identify what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 用化学方法把物质分解，以确定其成分
senses.example: The lab analysed the water samples for traces of lead.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室检测了水样中是否含铅。
senses.why: Chemistry took the 'loosening into parts' literally, so analyse can mean dissolving a sample into measurable components.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个「拆成部分」的动作照字面使用，所以 analyse 可以指把样本分解成可测量的成分。

senses.title: To treat by psychoanalysis
senses.definition: to treat a patient by exploring unconscious thoughts and feelings
senses.definitionCN: 通过探究无意识的思想与情感来治疗病人
senses.example: The patient was analysed by a Freudian therapist for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人接受了一位弗洛伊德派治疗师两年的精神分析。
senses.why: Psychoanalysis borrowed the word because it takes a mind apart into hidden drives, the same loosening applied to the psyche.
senses.whyCN: 精神分析借用这个词，是因为它把心灵拆解为隐藏的驱力，是同一套「拆松」用在心理层面。

intro.en: Analyse carries a Greek verb meaning to loosen, which is why analysis feels like taking something apart.
intro.cn: analyse 内含希腊语「解开」的动词，所以「分析」就像把东西拆开。

items.en: The prefix ana- meant 'up, throughout', giving a sense of thoroughness.
items.cn: 前缀 ana- 意为「向上、贯穿」，带来彻底性的意味。

items.en: lyein meant 'to loosen, to untie', the core of the word.
items.cn: lyein 意为「松开、解开」，是这个词的核心。

items.en: analyein meant 'to loosen up, to dissolve', used of both objects and arguments.
items.cn: analyein 意为「解开、分解」，既用于物体也用于论证。

items.en: The noun analysis passed into Latin and then into the modern languages.
items.cn: 名词 analysis 传入拉丁语，再进入现代各语言。

items.en: French formed the verb analyser, which English borrowed as analyse.
items.cn: 法语构成动词 analyser，英语借入为 analyse。

note.en: The look-alike group is the analysis family; the near-meaning group gives other ways of studying.
note.cn: 形近组是 analysis 词族；近义组给出其他研究方式。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
to cut something into parts for study
to judge the value of something

normalIntro.en: Analyse means to loosen a whole into its parts.
normalIntro.cn: analyse 就是把整体拆松成部分。

normal.en: The British spelling uses -yse, the American uses -yze.
normal.cn: 英式拼写用 -yse，美式用 -yze。

normal.en: The plural of the noun changes to analyses.
normal.cn: 名词复数写作 analyses。

normal.en: Analyse takes no preposition: analyse the data.
normal.cn: analyse 后直接接宾语，不加介词。

normal.en: The root lyein means to loosen.
normal.cn: 词根 lyein 意为松开。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-a-lyse.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-a-lyse。

abstract.en: Picture a clock opened on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上拆开的钟表。

abstract.en: See a water sample split into test tubes.
abstract.cn: 想象水样被分进试管。

abstract.en: Hear a therapist tracing a hidden memory.
abstract.cn: 听治疗师追溯一段隐藏的记忆。

examples.en: We need to analyse why sales fell last quarter.
examples.cn: 我们需要分析上季度销量下滑的原因。

examples.en: The technician analysed the soil for heavy metals.
examples.cn: 技术员化验了土壤中的重金属。

examples.en: The committee analysed the proposal line by line.
examples.cn: 委员会逐行分析了这份提案。

dict_mnemonic.text: ana 加 lyse（松开）：把整体松开成零件，就是分析。

root: 源自希腊语 analyein「解开、分解」，由 ana-「贯穿」与 lyein「松开」构成；名词 analysis 经拉丁语进入现代语言，法语再构成动词 analyser，英语借入为 analyse，另有美式拼写 analyze。

sensesIntro.en: Loosening a whole gives three uses: studying data, testing substances, and treating the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 把整体拆松生出三种用法：研究数据、化验物质、治疗心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock opened with its parts laid out.
core.cn: 核心意象：拆开的钟表与摊开的零件。

branches.en: a water sample tested for lead

intro.en: A Greek verb base with a family of nouns and adjectives in English.
intro.cn: 这是希腊动词词基，在英语中带出一族名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The word passed through Latin, which supplies the noun analysis.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经过拉丁语，拉丁语提供了名词 analysis。

definition_zh: 分析；分析报告；分解；精神分析
definition_en: a detailed examination of something by breaking it into parts, or the process of separating a substance or a mind
core_image: 白板上写着问题，箭头把原因一条条分开
scene: 报告开头先概述结论，第二部分才是对数据的详细分析。The second chapter offers a detailed analysis of the data.
sceneCN: 这里 analysis 是「分析」（第 1 个义项：把事物拆开来细看以理解其结构）；句意是第二章对数据作了详细分析。

pos.zh: 名词：分析；分析报告；分解

derivatives.zh: 形容词：分析的；善于分析的

senses.title: A detailed examination
senses.definition: a careful study of something that separates it into parts so that its nature can be understood
senses.definitionCN: 把事物分成各部分细加研究，以理解其性质
senses.example: The second chapter offers a detailed analysis of the data.
senses.exampleCN: 第二章对数据作了详细分析。
senses.why: The Greek noun meant 'a dissolving', so analysis names the act of breaking a whole down until its parts can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词意为「分解」，所以 analysis 指把整体拆开、直到各部分都能看清的动作。

senses.title: A chemical breakdown
senses.definition: the process of identifying the substances in a sample by separating them
senses.definitionCN: 通过分离来鉴定样本中所含物质的过程
senses.example: Chemical analysis showed traces of copper in the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 化学分析显示土壤中含有微量铜。
senses.why: Chemistry uses the literal sense of dissolving: the sample is separated into measurable components, and the report of that work is also called an analysis.
senses.whyCN: 化学用的是字面的「分解」义：样本被分离成可测量的成分，而这项工作的报告同样称为 analysis。

senses.title: Psychoanalysis
senses.definition: a method of treating mental distress by exploring unconscious feelings, or the theory behind it
senses.definitionCN: 通过探究无意识情感来治疗心理困扰的方法，或指其理论
senses.example: He underwent analysis for several years before training as a therapist.
senses.exampleCN: 他在接受治疗师训练之前做过几年精神分析。
senses.why: Freud's method takes the mind apart in the same way, so English uses the bare noun analysis for the treatment itself.
senses.whyCN: 弗洛伊德的方法也是以同样方式拆解心灵，因此英语直接用 analysis 这个词指这种治疗。

intro.en: Analysis is a Greek noun of dissolving, and every later sense keeps that knife-like quality.
intro.cn: analysis 是希腊语表示分解的名词，后来各义都保留着这种「下刀」的性质。

items.en: lyein meant 'to loosen, to untie', the verb at the heart of the word.
items.cn: lyein 意为「松开、解开」，是这个词的核心动词。

items.en: analysis meant 'a dissolving, a resolution into parts'.
items.cn: analysis 意为「分解、化为若干部分」。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun for logical and grammatical dissection.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该名词，用于逻辑与语法上的剖析。

items.en: English analysis first covered the resolving of things into their elements.
items.cn: 英语 analysis 最初指把事物分解为基本要素。

items.en: The word extended to chemical testing, economics, and Freudian psychoanalysis.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到化学检测、经济学与弗洛伊德精神分析。

note.en: The look-alike group tests singular and plural forms; the near-meaning group names kinds of study.
note.cn: 形近组分辨单复数形式；近义组列出不同研究方式。

entries.definition: a division into parts or categories
a piece of research on a subject

normalIntro.en: Analysis is the noun of loosening a whole into parts.
normalIntro.cn: analysis 是把整体拆松成部分的名词。

normal.en: One analysis, two analyses: the plural changes -is to -es.
normal.cn: 单数 analysis，复数 analyses，把 -is 变成 -es。

normal.en: In the final analysis means after all.
normal.cn: in the final analysis 意为归根结底。

normal.en: The verb is analyse in Britain, analyze in America.
normal.cn: 动词在英式是 analyse，美式是 analyze。

normal.en: Analysis is a noun, so do not write analyse here.
normal.cn: analysis 是名词，别在这里写成 analyse。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-NAL-y-sis.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-NAL-y-sis。

abstract.en: Picture arrows fanning out from one question.
abstract.cn: 想象从一个问题分出许多箭头。

abstract.en: See test tubes lined up after separation.
abstract.cn: 想象分离后排开的试管。

abstract.en: Hear a therapist and patient tracing a dream.
abstract.cn: 听治疗师与病人追索一个梦。

examples.en: The report includes an analysis of last year's spending.
examples.cn: 报告包含对去年支出的分析。

examples.en: Water analysis revealed unsafe levels of nitrate.
examples.cn: 水质分析显示硝酸盐超标。

examples.en: In the final analysis, the decision rests with the board.
examples.cn: 归根结底，决定权在董事会。

dict_mnemonic.text: ana 加 lysis（分解）：分解开来细看，就是分析。

root: 源自希腊语 analysis「分解」，其动词 lyein 意为松开、解开；经拉丁语进入英语，十六世纪指把事物分解为要素，后扩展到化学分析、经济分析与精神分析。

sensesIntro.en: The Greek sense of dissolving survives in three fields: general study, chemistry, and psychotherapy.
sensesIntro.cn: 希腊语的「分解」义在三个领域存续：一般研究、化学与心理治疗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question on a whiteboard with arrows to its causes.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上的问题引出多条原因箭头。

branches.cn: 多年的弗洛伊德式治疗

intro.en: A Greek noun whose -sis ending marks a process.
intro.cn: 这是希腊名词，-sis 词尾标示一个过程。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the noun, so both Greek and Latin forms are relevant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入了这个名词，因此希腊与拉丁形式都相关。

definition_zh: 分析师；化验员；精神分析学家
definition_en: a person who examines information or substances in detail, or a therapist trained in psychoanalysis
core_image: 屏幕前的人盯着密密麻麻的表格，用笔标出一处异常
scene: 公司季度报告发布前，分析师把三年的财务数据重新算了一遍。The analyst checked three years of accounts before the report.
sceneCN: 这里 analyst 是「分析师」（第 1 个义项：专门细查数据并给出判断的人）；句意是分析师在报告前复核了三年的账目。

pos.zh: 名词：分析师；化验员；精神分析学家

senses.title: One who studies data
senses.definition: a specialist whose job is to examine information closely and draw conclusions from it
senses.definitionCN: 以细查信息并从中得出结论为职业的专门人员
senses.example: The analyst checked three years of accounts before the report.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师在报告前复核了三年的账目。
senses.why: The -ist ending marks a person, so an analyst is simply the one who performs analysis, a role that became a profession in finance and business.
senses.whyCN: -ist 词尾标示人，所以 analyst 就是执行分析的人，这一角色在金融与商业中成为职业。

senses.title: One who tests substances
senses.definition: a person who carries out chemical or laboratory tests on samples
senses.definitionCN: 对样本进行化学或实验室检验的人
senses.example: The analyst found traces of mercury in the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 化验员在鱼中发现了微量汞。
senses.why: Because analysis includes chemical separation, the same title covers the laboratory worker who tests samples rather than markets.
senses.whyCN: 因为分析包含化学分解，同一个称谓也指检验样本的实验室人员，而不是研究市场的人。

senses.title: A psychoanalyst
senses.titleCN: 精神分析学家；精神分析师
senses.definition: a therapist trained to treat patients by exploring unconscious processes
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、通过探究无意识过程来治疗病人的治疗师
senses.example: She trained as an analyst in Vienna.
senses.exampleCN: 她在维也纳接受了精神分析师的训练。
senses.why: Psychoanalysis shortened its practitioner's title to analyst, especially in the phrase training analyst, so the word can mean a therapist.
senses.whyCN: 精神分析把从业者的头衔简称为 analyst，尤其在 training analyst 这类说法中，因此这个词也可以指治疗师。

intro.en: Analyst is the person-noun of analysis, and its job titles grew with the fields that used analysis.
intro.cn: analyst 是 analysis 的人物名词，其职业含义随着使用分析的领域而扩展。

items.en: The Greek noun meant 'a dissolving into parts'.
items.cn: 这个希腊名词意为「分解为若干部分」。

items.en: French formed analyste in the seventeenth century for one skilled in analysis.
items.cn: 法语在十七世纪构成 analyste，指擅长分析的人。

items.en: English analyst first named a person who analysed texts or arguments.
items.cn: 英语 analyst 最初指分析文本或论证的人。

items.en: Chemistry and finance gave the word its laboratory and market senses.
items.cn: 化学与金融赋予这个词实验室与市场两种职业含义。

items.en: Freudian practice made analyst a common short form for psychoanalyst.
items.cn: 弗洛伊德学派使 analyst 成为精神分析师的常用简称。

note.en: The look-alike group is the analysis family; the near-meaning group names related experts.
note.cn: 形近组是 analysis 词族；近义组列出相关专业人士。

entries.definition: a person who studies a subject in detail
a person who inspects or tests
a person trained to treat mental or physical problems

normalIntro.en: Analysis plus -ist: the person who does the analysis.
normalIntro.cn: analysis 加 -ist：做分析的那个人。

normal.en: -ist marks a person, as in artist and scientist.
normal.cn: -ist 标示人，如 artist 与 scientist。

normal.en: An analyst does not analyse for fun; it is a job.
normal.cn: analyst 的分析是职业，不只是兴趣。

normal.en: Psychoanalyst is often shortened to analyst.
normal.cn: psychoanalyst 常简称为 analyst。

normal.en: Financial analyst is the most common modern job title.
normal.cn: financial analyst 是现代最常见的职位名。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-a-lyst.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-a-lyst。

abstract.en: Picture a spreadsheet with one cell circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象表格里被红笔圈出的一格。

abstract.en: See a lab bench with labelled samples.
abstract.cn: 想象贴着标签的样品台。

abstract.en: Imagine a quiet consulting room and a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的诊室与一本笔记。

examples.en: The analyst expects inflation to fall next year.
examples.cn: 这位分析师预计明年通胀会下降。

examples.en: A laboratory analyst tested the milk for antibiotics.
examples.cn: 实验室化验员检测了牛奶中的抗生素。

examples.en: She has been an analyst for fifteen years.
examples.cn: 她做分析师已经十五年了。

dict_mnemonic.text: analysis（分析）加 -ist（人）：做分析的人，就是分析师。

root: 由 analysis 加人物后缀 -ist 构成，analysis 源自希腊语「分解」；十七世纪经法语 analyste 进入英语，最初指分析文本与论证的人，后随化学、金融与精神分析的发展获得多种职业含义。

sensesIntro.en: The person who analyses takes three professional shapes: data expert, lab tester, and therapist.
sensesIntro.cn: 做分析的人有三种职业形态：数据专家、实验室检验员与治疗师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure marking one anomaly in a wall of figures.
core.cn: 核心意象：在满屏数字中标出一处异常的人。

branches.cn: 复核账目的金融分析师

intro.en: A person-noun built on analysis with the Greek -ist ending.
intro.cn: 这是用希腊 -ist 词尾加在 analysis 上的人物名词。

latinIntro.en: The base analysis passed through Latin; the following entries trace it.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 analysis 经过拉丁语，下面列出相关词条。

definition_zh: 祖先；祖宗；（事物的）前身
definition_en: a person from whom one is descended, or an earlier thing from which a later one developed
core_image: 泛黄的族谱上，一代代名字向上延伸
scene: 家里的老相册第一页，是一位从南方迁来的曾祖父。Her ancestors came from a fishing village in the south.
sceneCN: 这里 ancestor 是「祖先」（第 1 个义项：血缘上的先辈）；句意是她的祖先来自南方一个渔村。

derivatives.zh: 名词：前身；先行词，同源于拉丁语「在前」

senses.title: A forebear in the family
senses.definition: a person in one's family line who lived long ago
senses.definitionCN: 家族血脉中生活在很久以前的先辈
senses.example: Her ancestors came from a fishing village in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖先来自南方一个渔村。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin antecessor, 'one who goes before', so an ancestor is literally a person who walked ahead of us in time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语 antecessor「走在前面的人」，所以祖先字面上就是在时间上走在我们前面的人。

senses.title: An earlier form of a thing
senses.definition: an early version or forerunner from which a later thing developed
senses.definitionCN: 后来事物由之发展而来的早期形态或先驱
senses.example: The abacus is an ancestor of the modern calculator.
senses.exampleCN: 算盘是现代计算器的前身。
senses.why: Once the word means 'what came before', it can be applied to machines and ideas, not only to people, which is common in histories of technology.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「先前存在的东西」，它就能用于机器与观念，而不只用于人，这在技术史中很常见。

intro.en: Ancestor is a Latin 'one who goes before', filtered through French.
intro.cn: ancestor 是拉丁语「走在前面的人」，经法语传入英语。

items.en: ante meant 'before', in place or in time.
items.cn: ante 意为「在前」，指位置或时间。

items.en: cedere meant 'to go, to yield', the verb of movement.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让」，是表示移动的动词。

items.en: antecessor meant 'a predecessor, one who goes before'.
items.cn: antecessor 意为「前任、走在前头的人」。

items.en: French reshaped the word as ancestre, and English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语把词形改造为 ancestre，英语借入。

items.en: English ancestor first meant a family forebear, then extended to forerunners of machines and species.
items.cn: 英语 ancestor 先指家族先辈，后扩展到机器与物种的前身。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ancestry family; the near-meaning group contrasts forebear and descendant.
note.cn: 形近组是 ancestry 词族；近义组对比先辈与后代。

entries.definition: a person or thing that came before
a person descended from an ancestor

normalIntro.en: An ancestor is one who went before us.
normalIntro.cn: 祖先就是走在我们前面的人。

normal.en: Ante- means before, as in antecedent.
normal.cn: ante- 意为在前，如 antecedent。

normal.en: Ancestor is a person, ancestry is the line.
normal.cn: ancestor 是人，ancestry 是世系。

normal.en: Ancestral home is the family's old place.
normal.cn: ancestral home 指祖居。

normal.en: Machines can have ancestors too.
normal.cn: 机器也可以有「前身」。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-ces-tor.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-ces-tor。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree climbing upward.
abstract.cn: 想象向上延伸的族谱。

abstract.en: See an old photograph of a great-grandfather.
abstract.cn: 想象一张曾祖父的旧照片。

abstract.en: Imagine an abacus beside a calculator.
abstract.cn: 想象算盘放在计算器旁边。

examples.en: Her ancestors arrived here two centuries ago.
examples.cn: 她的祖先两个世纪前来到这里。

examples.en: Humans and apes share a common ancestor.
examples.cn: 人类与猿类有共同祖先。

examples.en: The steam engine is an ancestor of the modern turbine.
examples.cn: 蒸汽机是现代涡轮机的前身。

dict_mnemonic.text: ante（在前）加 cess（走）加 -or（人）：走在前面的人，就是祖先。

root: 源自拉丁语 antecessor「走在前头的人」，由 ante「在前」与 cedere「走」构成，经古法语 ancestre 进入英语；本指家族先辈，后引申为事物或物种的前身。

sensesIntro.en: The one who goes before can be a family member or an earlier machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 「走在前面者」既可以是家族成员，也可以是更早的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a family tree rising into old photographs.
core.cn: 核心意象：族谱向上延伸进旧照片。

branches.en: the steam engine before the turbine

intro.en: A Latin compound of before and going, reshaped by French.
intro.cn: 这是拉丁语「在前」与「走」的复合词，经法语改造。

latinIntro.en: The Latin elements ante and cedere are listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 下面列出拉丁成分 ante 与 cedere。

definition_zh: 锚；使固定；新闻主播；（精神上的）支柱
definition_en: a heavy device dropped from a boat to hold it in place, the act of fixing something firmly, or a person who presents the news
core_image: 一只铁锚沉入海底，缆绳绷紧，船停住了
scene: 风浪里，船长把船开到海湾，抛下锚等天亮。They anchored the boat in the bay until the storm passed.
sceneCN: 这里 anchor 是「抛锚；使固定」（第 2 个义项：作动词，用锚把船固定住）；句意是他们把船停在湾里抛锚，直到风暴过去。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：未固定的；无依无靠的

senses.title: The device that holds a ship
senses.definition: a heavy metal object dropped from a ship so that its weight and grip on the seabed hold the ship in place
senses.definitionCN: 从船上沉入水底的重金属物，凭重量与抓力把船固定在原处
senses.example: The ship let down its anchor outside the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船在港口外抛下了锚。
senses.why: The word came into English from Greek and Latin names for the same iron hook, so the object has kept its name for more than a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经由希腊语与拉丁语中指同一铁钩的名称进入英语，所以这个物件一千多年来都叫同一个名字。

senses.title: To fix something in place
senses.definition: to hold a boat or an object firmly in one position
senses.definitionCN: 把船或物体牢牢固定在某个位置
senses.example: They anchored the boat in the bay until the storm passed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把船停在海湾里抛锚，直到风暴过去。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb because anchoring is an action, and from boats the verb spread to any object fixed firmly to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，是因为「抛锚」是一个动作；从船只开始，这个动词扩展到任何被牢牢固定在地面的物体。

senses.title: A mainstay or news presenter
senses.definition: a person who gives stability to a group or programme, especially the presenter who holds a news broadcast together
senses.definitionCN: 给团体或节目提供稳定性的人，尤指串联整档新闻的主播
senses.example: She has been the anchor of the evening news for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 她主持晚间新闻已经十年了。
senses.why: A news anchor holds a programme in place the way an anchor holds a ship, and the same metaphor extends to a family's steady centre.
senses.whyCN: 新闻主播稳住一档节目，就像锚稳住一艘船；同样的比喻也延伸到家庭中那个稳定的中心人物。

intro.en: Anchor is an ancient sea word, borrowed from Greek through Latin and into Old English.
intro.cn: anchor 是古老的航海词，经拉丁语从希腊语借入古英语。

items.en: ankyra meant 'anchor', and it is also the source of the medical word ankylosis.
items.cn: ankyra 意为「锚」，也是医学术语 ankylosis 的来源。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as ancora, the term used by sailors.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 ancora，是水手使用的说法。

items.en: Old English took the word from Latin and used it for the iron hook.
items.cn: 古英语从拉丁语借入 ancor，指铁锚。

items.en: The spelling shifted towards anchor under Latin influence.
items.cn: 在拉丁语影响下，拼写逐渐变为 anchor。

items.en: The figurative senses grew in broadcasting and in everyday talk about stability.
items.cn: 比喻义在广播行业与日常谈「稳定」时发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sea root; the near-meaning group gives mooring and support words.
note.cn: 形近组共享航海词根；近义组给出停泊与支撑类词。

entries.definition: a place where ships may anchor
to tie a boat to the shore

normalIntro.en: An anchor holds a ship the way a mainstay holds a family.
normalIntro.cn: 锚稳住船，就像支柱稳住家庭。

normal.en: Drop anchor to stop, weigh anchor to leave.
normal.cn: drop anchor 是抛锚停下，weigh anchor 是起锚离开。

normal.en: The news anchor holds the programme together.
normal.cn: 新闻主播把整档节目串联起来。

normal.en: Anchor is both a noun and a verb.
normal.cn: anchor 既是名词也是动词。

normal.en: Greek ankyra is the oldest form we can trace.
normal.cn: 可追溯的最早形式是希腊语 ankyra。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-chor.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-chor。

abstract.en: Picture an iron hook biting into the seabed.
abstract.cn: 想象铁钩咬进海底。

abstract.en: See a taut rope and a still boat.
abstract.cn: 想象绷紧的缆绳与停稳的船。

abstract.en: Imagine a presenter holding a broadcast steady.
abstract.cn: 想象主播稳住一整档直播。

examples.en: They dropped anchor just outside the reef.
examples.cn: 他们就在礁石外抛了锚。

examples.en: The tent was anchored to the ground with strong ropes.
examples.cn: 帐篷用粗绳固定在地上。

examples.en: He became the anchor of the morning news programme.
examples.cn: 他成了早间新闻节目的主播。

dict_mnemonic.text: anchor 听起来像「安可」：把船安好、可停稳，靠的就是锚。

root: 源自希腊语 ankyra「锚」，经拉丁语 ancora 与古英语 ancor 进入英语，拼写在拉丁语影响下变为 anchor；由实物的锚引申出「固定」的动词义，以及新闻主播、家庭支柱等比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: One iron hook gives three uses: the object, the act of fixing, and the person who steadies things.
sensesIntro.cn: 一只铁锚生出三种用法：物件本身、固定的动作，以及稳住局面的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron hook biting into the seabed.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁钩咬住海底。

branches.en: a tent roped to the ground
a boat held through a storm
the anchor of the evening news

intro.en: A Greek sea word with a small English family and a strong figurative life.
intro.cn: 这是希腊航海词，英语中有一小族词，比喻用法也很活跃。

latinIntro.en: Latin ancora is the bridge between Greek and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ancora 是希腊语与英语之间的桥梁。

items.meaning: a device to hold a ship

items.example: an anchor point for the rope

definition_zh: 古代的；古老的；古人（复数名词）
definition_en: belonging to the distant past, extremely old, or the people who lived in ancient times
core_image: 阳光下断成几截的石柱，浮雕已被风磨平
scene: 博物馆里，孩子们围着一尊三千年前的石像听讲解。The museum displays pottery from ancient Egypt.
sceneCN: 这里 ancient 是「古代的」（第 1 个义项：属于遥远的过去）；句意是博物馆展出古埃及的陶器。

derivatives.zh: 名词：古代；古物，同源于拉丁语「在前」
名词：古董；形容词：古老的
名词：祖先，同源于拉丁语「在前」

senses.title: Of the distant past
senses.definition: belonging to the period of history before the Middle Ages, especially Greece and Rome
senses.definitionCN: 属于中世纪以前的历史时期，尤指希腊与罗马
senses.example: The museum displays pottery from ancient Egypt.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出古埃及的陶器。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it means 'before', so ancient marks what belongs to the time that came before the familiar eras of history.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁词意为「在前的」，所以 ancient 标示属于我们熟悉的历史时期之前那个时代的事物。

senses.title: Very old
senses.definition: having existed for a very long time, used of things, customs, or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 已存在很久，用于事物、习俗或制度
senses.example: The village keeps an ancient custom of lighting fires in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄保留着春天点火的古老习俗。
senses.why: Because 'before' can be measured from the speaker rather than from an era, ancient also simply means older than memory, even without a date.
senses.whyCN: 因为「在前」可以从说话人而非某个时代来量度，所以 ancient 也可以只表示比记忆更久远，不必有确切年代。

senses.title: The people of old
senses.definition: the people who lived in ancient times, especially their writers and thinkers
senses.definitionCN: 生活在古代的人，尤指其中的作家与思想家
senses.example: The ancients knew the stars better than we often assume.
senses.exampleCN: 古人对星辰的了解比我们通常以为的更多。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the people it describes, a common shift that lets English speak of the ancients as a collective.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成指其所描述之人的名词，这是常见的转变，使英语可以用 the ancients 统称古人。

intro.en: Ancient began as a French word for 'before', and its final -t was added by mistake.
intro.cn: ancient 最初是法语中表示「在先」的词，词尾的 -t 是后来误加上的。

items.en: ante meant 'before', in both space and time.
items.cn: ante 意为「在前」，可指空间也可指时间。

items.en: ancien meant 'old, former, belonging to earlier times'.
items.cn: ancien 意为「旧的、从前的、属于早先时代的」。

items.en: English borrowed the word as auncient, later spelled ancient.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入为 auncient，后来拼作 ancient。

items.en: The final -t was added by analogy with words such as pageant and tyrant.
items.cn: 词尾 -t 是仿照 pageant、tyrant 等词加上的。

items.en: Ancient now covers both the classical past and anything extremely old.
items.cn: 现代 ancient 既指古典时代，也指任何极其古老的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'before' root; the near-meaning group grades age.
note.cn: 形近组共享「在前」词根；近义组按年代远近分级。

entries.definition: an object from an earlier period
having lived or existed a long time
existing for a very long time
belonging to the time before written records

normalIntro.en: Ancient comes from ante, before: the age before ours.
normalIntro.cn: ancient 来自 ante「在前」：我们之前的时代。

normal.en: Ante- means before, as in ante meridiem.
normal.cn: ante- 意为在前，如 ante meridiem。

normal.en: Ancient history ends where the Middle Ages begin.
normal.cn: 古代史在中世纪开始处结束。

normal.en: The ancients means the people of that age.
normal.cn: the ancients 指那个时代的人。

normal.en: Do not confuse ancient with antique.
normal.cn: 别把 ancient 与 antique 混用。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-cient.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-cient。

abstract.en: Picture broken columns under bright sun.
abstract.cn: 想象烈日下断裂的石柱。

abstract.en: See a glass case holding old pottery.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜里的古老陶器。

abstract.en: Imagine a spring fire lit by custom for centuries.
abstract.cn: 想象沿袭数百年的春季篝火。

examples.en: Ancient Rome once ruled most of the Mediterranean.
examples.cn: 古罗马曾统治地中海的大部分地区。

examples.en: The path follows an ancient route across the hills.

sensesIntro.en: The era before ours, anything older than memory, and the people of that era.
sensesIntro.cn: 我们之前的时代、比记忆更久远的事物，以及那个时代的人。

latinIntro.en: The Latin preposition ante is the historical anchor of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁介词 ante 是这一词族的历史锚点。

definition_zh: 和；与；然后；加
definition_en: used to join words, phrases, or clauses, to show a sequence of actions, or to add numbers
core_image: 两只手被一根短绳连在一起
scene: 清单上写着要买面包、牛奶和鸡蛋三样东西。We need bread, milk and eggs.
sceneCN: 这里 and 是「和」（第 1 个义项：连接并列的词或短语）；句意是我们要买面包、牛奶和鸡蛋。

derivatives.zh: 名词：& 符号，原意为「and per se and」
介词：加，义近 and 的算术用法
副词：也，义近 and 的补充作用
限定词：两者都，常与 and 搭配

senses.title: Joining words or things
senses.definition: used to connect two or more words, phrases, or clauses of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 用于连接两个或更多同类词、短语或分句
senses.example: We need bread, milk and eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要面包、牛奶和鸡蛋。
senses.why: The oldest use of and is simply to link equals, a job it has done since Old English without change.
senses.whyCN: and 最古老的用法就是连接对等成分，这个功能从古英语至今没有改变。

senses.title: Showing what happens next
senses.titleCN: 然后；接着（连接先后动作）
senses.definition: used between two actions to show that the second follows the first
senses.definitionCN: 用于两个动作之间，表示后者紧接前者发生
senses.example: She opened the door and walked in.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开门，走了进去。
senses.why: When and joins two verbs of action, the order of the words becomes the order of events, so the conjunction carries a sense of sequence.
senses.whyCN: 当 and 连接两个动作动词时，词的先后就成了事件的先后，于是这个连词带上了时间顺序的意味。

senses.title: Adding numbers
senses.definition: used between numbers to mean that they are added together
senses.definitionCN: 用于数字之间，表示把它们相加
senses.example: Two and three makes five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: Arithmetic treats 'joining' in the plainest way: put two quantities together and the result is their sum.
senses.whyCN: 算术把「连接」照最直白的方式使用：把两个数量放在一起，结果就是它们的和。

intro.en: And is one of the oldest words in English, unchanged in meaning for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: and 是英语中最古老的词之一，一千多年来词义未变。

items.en: A Germanic form meaning 'and, also' lay behind the Old English word.
items.cn: 古英语词背后有一个意为「和、也」的日耳曼语形式。

items.en: and or ond joined words and clauses exactly as it does today.
items.cn: and 或 ond 连接词与分句的方式与今天完全相同。

items.en: The variant ond was common in early texts before and became standard.
items.cn: 较早文本中常见 ond 这一变体，后来 and 成为标准。

items.en: Spelling settled as and, and the reduced form 'n' appeared in compounds such as rock'n'roll.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 and，缩略形式 'n' 出现在 rock'n'roll 等组合中。

items.en: Modern grammar keeps and for coordination, sequence, and arithmetic.
items.cn: 现代语法保留 and 的并列、顺承与算术用法。

note.en: The look-alike group separates and from similar short words; the near-meaning group gives connectors.
note.cn: 形近组区分 and 与形似的短词；近义组列出连接成分。

normalIntro.en: And is the shortest bridge between two things.
normalIntro.cn: and 是两样东西之间最短的桥。

normal.en: And joins equals, not unequals.
normal.cn: and 连接的是对等成分。

normal.en: Two actions joined by and happen in that order.
normal.cn: and 连接的两个动作按顺序发生。

normal.en: In arithmetic, and means plus.

normal.en: The ampersand is a stylised and.
normal.cn: & 符号是 and 的花体写法。

abstract.en: Hear a door open, then footsteps.
abstract.cn: 听到门开，然后是脚步。

examples.cn: 她买了一张地图和一瓶水。

examples.en: Four and six makes ten.
examples.cn: 四加六等于十。

root: 源自古英语 and 与 ond，可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「和、也」的形式；一千多年来始终用于连接对等成分，并由并列引申出顺承与算术相加的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Joining equals, ordering actions, and adding numbers are three faces of one link.
sensesIntro.cn: 连接对等、排定先后、数字相加，是同一个连接动作的三面。

intro.cn: 这是日耳曼语核心功能词，所谓构词家族其实是它的连接词伙伴。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 愤怒；怒气；使发怒
definition_en: a strong feeling of displeasure, or to make someone feel that way
core_image: 紧握的拳头和发红的耳根
scene: 听到对方又一次推卸责任，他压不住怒火，站了起来。His anger rose when the blame was passed to him again.
sceneCN: 这里 anger 是「愤怒」（第 1 个义项：作名词，强烈的恼怒情绪）；句意是当责任又被推到他身上时，他的怒火升了起来。

derivatives.zh: 名词：极度痛苦，与 anger 同源
名词：心绞痛，同源于「收紧」之义

senses.title: The feeling of rage
senses.definition: a strong emotion caused by a wrong, an insult, or frustration
senses.definitionCN: 因受到不公、侮辱或挫折而产生的强烈情绪
senses.example: His anger rose when the blame was passed to him again.
senses.exampleCN: 当责任又被推到他身上时，他的怒火升了起来。
senses.why: The word came from Old Norse angr, 'grief, trouble', so anger began as a tight, painful distress before it narrowed to rage.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古北欧语 angr「悲痛、困扰」，所以 anger 最初是一种紧绷而痛苦的难受，后来才收窄为暴怒。

senses.title: To make someone angry
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel strong displeasure
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生强烈的恼怒
senses.example: The delay angered passengers who had already waited an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 延误激怒了已经等了一小时的乘客。
senses.why: Since the noun names the feeling, the verb simply says that someone has been made to feel it, a pattern common with emotion words.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词指这种情绪，动词就表示使人产生这种情绪，这是情感词常见的构词方式。

intro.en: Anger came from the north with the Vikings, and it first meant grief rather than rage.
intro.cn: anger 随维京人从北方传入，最初意为悲痛而非暴怒。

items.en: angr meant 'grief, sorrow, trouble', with a sense of tightness.
items.cn: angr 意为「悲痛、忧伤、困扰」，带有紧绷之感。

items.en: The related form angh meant 'tight, narrow', the physical root of the feeling.
items.cn: 相关形式 angh 意为「紧的、窄的」，是这种情绪的身体根源。

items.en: English angre first meant 'distress, affliction' rather than wrath.
items.cn: 英语 angre 最初意为「痛苦、折磨」，而不是暴怒。

items.en: The sense shifted towards 'resentment and wrath' as the word entered everyday use.
items.cn: 随着日常使用增加，词义转向「怨恨与暴怒」。

items.en: Modern anger is the plain word for rage, with angry and angrily built on it.
items.cn: 现代 anger 是表示暴怒的常用词，并派生出 angry 与 angrily。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tightness root; the near-meaning group grades intensity.
note.cn: 形近组共享「紧绷」词根；近义组按强度分级。

normalIntro.en: Anger began as a tight, painful grief.
normalIntro.cn: anger 最初是一种紧绷而痛苦的悲伤。

normal.cn: 古北欧语 angr 意为悲痛。

normal.en: Anger is the noun, angry the adjective.

abstract.en: Imagine a chest tight with grief.
abstract.cn: 想象因悲痛而发紧的胸口。

examples.en: She spoke to him in anger and later apologized.
examples.cn: 她愤怒地对他说话，后来道了歉。

examples.en: He could not hide his anger at the unfair decision.
examples.cn: 他无法掩饰对这项不公决定的气愤。

examples.en: The comments angered many local residents.
examples.cn: 这些言论激怒了许多当地居民。

dict_mnemonic.text: anger 与 anguish 同源，都指胸口发紧的难受，后来专指愤怒。

root: 源自古北欧语 angr「悲痛、困扰」，与表示「紧、窄」的 angh 相关，经中古英语 angre 进入英语；词义由「痛苦、折磨」逐渐转向「怨恨与暴怒」，并派生出 angry、angrily。

sensesIntro.en: The feeling and the act of causing it are the two sides of one word.
sensesIntro.cn: 这种情绪本身与使人产生这种情绪，是同一个词的两面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clenched fist and a tight chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：紧握的拳头与发紧的胸口。

intro.cn: 这是北欧语借词，其词根还产生了 anguish 与 angina。

definition_zh: 角；角度；视角；斜向；钓鱼
definition_en: the space between two meeting lines, a way of looking at something, or to fish with a hook
core_image: 两条直线在顶点相交，形成一个张开的角
scene: 摄影师蹲下来，从很低的角度拍那栋楼，线条一下变得有力。She shot the building from a low angle.
sceneCN: 这里 angle 是「角度」（第 2 个义项：观察或拍摄的方向）；句意是她从低角度拍摄这栋楼。

pos.zh: 动词：斜向移动；钓鱼；谋求

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有角的；棱角分明的

senses.title: The space between lines
senses.definition: the figure formed where two lines or surfaces meet, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 两条线或两个面相交处形成的图形，以度数计量
senses.example: The two walls meet at a right angle.
senses.exampleCN: 两面墙以直角相接。
senses.why: Latin angulus meant 'corner', so the geometric sense is the oldest: the word names the bend where two lines meet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angulus 意为「角、拐角」，所以几何义最古老：这个词指两条线相交处的那个弯。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.definition: a particular way of considering a situation or presenting a story
senses.definitionCN: 考虑问题或叙述事情的特定方式
senses.example: She shot the building from a low angle.
senses.exampleCN: 她从低角度拍摄了这栋楼。
senses.why: A corner gives a particular view of a room, so angle came to mean the position from which something is seen or judged.
senses.whyCN: 站在一个角落能看到房间的特定一面，所以 angle 引申为观察或判断事物的位置。

senses.title: To fish or to scheme
senses.definition: to fish with a hook, or to try to get something indirectly, as in angle for an invitation
senses.definitionCN: 用鱼钩钓鱼，或间接地谋求某物，如拐弯抹角地讨邀请
senses.example: They angled for trout in the cold stream.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在冰冷的溪流里钓鳟鱼。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different Old English word, angel, 'fishhook', which happened to merge in spelling with the geometric angle.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个古英语词 angel「鱼钩」，只是拼写恰好与几何义的 angle 合流。

intro.en: Angle is really two words in one coat: a Latin corner and an Old English fishhook.
intro.cn: angle 其实是两件外衣穿在一个词里：拉丁语的「角」与古英语的「鱼钩」。

items.en: angulus meant 'corner, bend', the source of the geometric sense.
items.cn: angulus 意为「角、弯」，是几何义的来源。

items.en: angel meant 'fishhook', a separate word that later shared the spelling angle.
items.cn: angel 意为「鱼钩」，是后来与 angle 共用拼写的另一个词。

items.en: French passed the Latin corner word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语把拉丁语的「角」于十四世纪传入英语。

items.en: The fishing sense settled under the same spelling, and the verb to angle appeared.
items.cn: 钓鱼义在同一拼写下固定，动词 angle 也随之出现。

items.en: Modern English uses angle for geometry, viewpoint, and indirect seeking, while angler keeps the fishing link.
items.cn: 现代英语用 angle 表示几何角、视角与间接谋求，而 angler 保留钓鱼的联系。

note.en: The look-alike group warns about angel; the near-meaning group gives viewpoint words.
note.cn: 形近组提醒与 angel 的区别；近义组列视角类词。

abstract.en: Imagine a line cast into a cold stream.
abstract.cn: 想象鱼线抛进冰冷的溪水。

intro.en: A Latin corner word that also absorbed an Old English fishhook.

definition_zh: 愤怒地；气冲冲地
definition_en: in a way that shows anger
core_image: 门被用力带上，脚步声急促远去
scene: 她把手里的文件往桌上一放，转身就走，没说一句话。She left the room angrily without a word.
sceneCN: 这里 angrily 是「愤怒地」（第 1 个义项：以显出怒气的样子做某事）；句意是她一言不发地愤怒离开房间。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：更生气的，angry 的比较级
形容词：最生气的，angry 的最高级

senses.title: In an angry manner
senses.definition: doing something in a way that clearly shows anger
senses.definitionCN: 以明显显出怒气的方式做某事
senses.example: She left the room angrily without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她一言不发地愤然离开房间。
senses.why: The -ly form of angry describes the manner of an action, so angrily tells you how someone spoke, looked, or moved, not how they felt inside.
senses.whyCN: angry 的 -ly 形式描述动作方式，所以 angrily 说明某人说话、看人或走动的样子，而不是内心的感受。

senses.title: With violent force, in description
senses.titleCN: 猛烈地；狂暴地（拟人描写）
senses.definition: used of wind, water, or weather that seems to act with anger in literary description
senses.definitionCN: 文学描写中形容风、水或天气仿佛带着怒气般猛烈
senses.example: The wind blew angrily through the empty streets.
senses.exampleCN: 风在空荡的街道上怒号。
senses.why: Writers transfer human anger to nature, so angrily can describe a storm's force as if it were a temper.
senses.whyCN: 作家把人的愤怒移到自然身上，于是 angrily 可以把风暴的猛烈写成仿佛有脾气。

intro.en: Angrily is angry with its y changed to i and an -ly added.
intro.cn: angrily 就是 angry 把词尾 y 改成 i 再加 -ly。

items.en: angr meant 'grief, distress', the distant source of the family.
items.cn: angr 意为「悲痛、痛苦」，是这一词族的远源。

items.en: anger shifted from distress to wrath.
items.cn: anger 从痛苦转向暴怒。

items.en: The adjective angry was formed with -y, meaning 'full of anger'.
items.cn: 形容词 angry 由 -y 构成，意为「充满怒气的」。

items.en: The adverb angrily appears, with y changing to i before -ly.
items.cn: 副词 angrily 出现，y 在 -ly 前变为 i。

items.en: Angrily is now the standard adverb for speech and behaviour that shows anger.
items.cn: 现代 angrily 是表示言语与行为显露怒气的标准副词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anger family; the near-meaning group gives other angry adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 anger 词族；近义组给出其他表示愤怒的副词。

normalIntro.en: Angry plus -ly, with y turned into i: angrily.
normalIntro.cn: angry 加 -ly，y 变 i：angrily。

normal.en: Adjectives ending in y change y to i before -ly.
normal.cn: 以 y 结尾的形容词加 -ly 时把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: Angrily describes the action, anger the feeling.
normal.cn: angrily 描述动作，anger 描述情绪。

normal.en: Speak angrily is the most common collocation.
normal.cn: speak angrily 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Do not write angryly; the i is required.
normal.cn: 不要写成 angryly，必须用 i。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-gri-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-gri-ly。

abstract.en: Picture a door slammed hard.
abstract.cn: 想象门被重重带上。

abstract.en: See papers dropped on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象文件被拍在桌上。

abstract.en: Hear wind rattling an empty street.
abstract.cn: 听到风在空街上作响。

examples.en: He replied angrily that the decision was unfair.
examples.cn: 他气愤地回答说这个决定不公平。

examples.en: The crowd shouted angrily at the referee.
examples.cn: 人群愤怒地朝裁判喊叫。

examples.en: She stared angrily at the broken window.
examples.cn: 她气愤地盯着破碎的窗户。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb covers human behaviour and, in literature, the violence of weather.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词既写人的行为，也在文学中写天气的猛烈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slammed door and quick footsteps.
core.cn: 核心意象：被摔上的门与急促的脚步。

intro.en: A regular -ly adverb, useful for showing how an emotion surfaces in action.
intro.cn: 这是规则的 -ly 副词，用于表现情绪如何显露在动作中。

latinIntro.en: The base is Norse rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自北欧语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 生气的；愤怒的；（风雨等）狂暴的
definition_en: feeling or showing anger about a person or situation; also used of weather that looks dark and violent
core_image: 攥紧的拳头与绷紧的下颌
scene: 他把没喝完的咖啡重重放回桌上，转身不再说话。He was angry with his brother for breaking the promise.
sceneCN: 这里 angry 是「生气的」（第 1 个义项：对某人怀有怒意）；句意是他因弟弟违背承诺而生他的气。

pos.zh: 形容词：生气的；愤怒的；狂暴的

derivatives.zh: 名词：易怒；怒气，较少使用

senses.title: Feeling anger towards a person
senses.definition: feeling or showing anger because of something a particular person has done
senses.definitionCN: 因某个特定的人做过的事而感到或显出怒气
senses.example: He was angry with his brother for breaking the promise.
senses.exampleCN: 他因弟弟违背承诺而生他的气。
senses.why: Angry is the adjective built from anger with -y, so it names a person who is full of that emotion and directs it at someone.
senses.whyCN: angry 由 anger 加 -y 构成，指满含这种情绪并把怒气指向某个人的人。

senses.title: Angry about a situation
senses.definition: feeling anger about an event, situation, or state of affairs rather than at a person
senses.definitionCN: 对事件、局面或状况感到愤怒，而不是针对某个人
senses.example: Many residents are angry about the sudden rise in rents.
senses.exampleCN: 许多居民对租金突然上涨感到愤怒。
senses.why: English splits the target of anger: with points at a person, while about or at points at a state of affairs.
senses.whyCN: 英语把怒气的对象分开：with 指向人，about 或 at 指向事情的状况。

senses.title: Violent, as of weather
senses.definition: used of wind, sea, or sky that looks dark and violent, as if it were in a temper
senses.definitionCN: 形容风、海或天空阴沉猛烈，仿佛带着脾气
senses.example: Dark angry clouds gathered over the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 阴沉狂暴的乌云在山间聚集。
senses.why: The metaphor treats a storm as a living temper, so the adjective for human rage is lent to the sky.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把风暴当作活物的脾气，于是写人发怒的形容词被借给了天空。

intro.en: Angry belongs to a Norse family that began with grief, not rage.
intro.cn: angry 属于一个源自北欧语的词族，最初的意思是悲痛而非暴怒。

items.en: angr meant 'grief, sorrow', and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: angr 意为「悲痛、忧伤」，是整族词的根源。

items.en: anger entered English meaning distress and trouble before it came to mean wrath.
items.cn: anger 进入英语时意为痛苦与困扰，后来才转为暴怒。

items.en: The adjective was formed with -y, meaning 'full of anger'.
items.cn: 形容词由 -y 构成，意为「充满怒气的」。

items.en: Angry is recorded in the fourteenth century; the split between with and about settled later.
items.cn: angry 在十四世纪已有记录，with 与 about 的分工是后来才定下的。

items.en: The weather sense developed in literary use and is now common in description.
items.cn: 天气义在文学用法中发展起来，如今在描写中很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anger family; the near-meaning group grades the strength of the feeling.
note.cn: 形近组是 anger 词族；近义组按情绪强度分级。

entries.definition: in a way that shows anger
mildly angry, used in British speech

normalIntro.en: Angry is anger plus -y, and y turns to i before -er and -est.
normalIntro.cn: angry 是 anger 加 -y，在 -er 与 -est 前 y 变为 i。

normal.en: Angry equals anger plus -y, 'full of anger'.
normal.cn: angry 等于 anger 加 -y，意为「充满怒气的」。

normal.en: Be angry with a person, angry about a thing.
normal.cn: 对人生气用 with，对事发怒用 about。

normal.en: The comparative is angrier, not more angry in most writing.
normal.cn: 比较级通常写 angrier，多数书面语不用 more angry。

normal.en: An angry sky warns of a coming storm.
normal.cn: angry sky 预示风暴将至。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: ANG-ry.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：ANG-ry。

abstract.en: See a fist tightening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头慢慢攥紧。

abstract.en: Hear a door slam shut.
abstract.cn: 听到门被重重关上。

abstract.en: Feel the heat rising in your face.
abstract.cn: 感到脸上腾起的热意。

examples.en: She was angry with herself for forgetting the appointment.
examples.cn: 她因忘记约定而生自己的气。

examples.en: The coach was angry about the team's careless mistakes.
examples.cn: 教练对球队粗心的失误感到恼火。

examples.en: Angry waves crashed against the harbour wall.
examples.cn: 狂暴的浪拍打着港口堤墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: anger（愤怒）加 -y（充满……的）：生气的；发怒的。

root: 由名词 anger 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，意为「充满怒气的」；anger 源自古北欧语 angr「悲痛」，中古英语时期词义由痛苦转为愤怒，与 angrily、angriness 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Three uses: anger at a person, anger at a situation, and a literary storm.
sensesIntro.cn: 三种用法：对人生气、对事感到愤怒，以及文学中的风暴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clenched fist and a tight jaw.
core.cn: 核心意象：攥紧的拳头与绷紧的下颌。

intro.en: A native adjective formed with -y from a noun of emotion, with a regular comparative.
intro.cn: 这是一个由情绪名词加 -y 构成的本族形容词，比较级规则变化。

latinIntro.en: The base is Norse rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自北欧语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 动物；兽类；动物的；肉体的
definition_en: a living creature that is not a plant, especially one other than a human being; also the adjective for what belongs to such creatures or to the body
core_image: 田里一头牛抬头望向人的方向
scene: 孩子趴在栏杆前，一只只数着围场里的牲畜。The children watched every animal in the field.
sceneCN: 这里 animal 是「动物」（第 1 个义项：与植物相对的生物）；句意是孩子们看着田里的每一只动物。

derivatives.zh: 动词：使有生气；形容词：有生命的

senses.title: A living creature
senses.definition: a living thing that can move about and feed itself, as opposed to a plant
senses.definitionCN: 能移动并自行取食的生物，与植物相对
senses.example: The children watched every animal in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们看着田里的每一只动物。
senses.why: Animal comes from Latin anima, 'breath, soul', because a living creature was defined as the thing that breathes.
senses.whyCN: animal 来自拉丁语 anima「气息、灵魂」，因为活物曾被定义为会呼吸的东西。

senses.title: A non-human creature
senses.definition: a creature other than a human being, especially a mammal
senses.definitionCN: 人以外的生物，尤指哺乳动物
senses.example: The zoo keeps animals from every continent.
senses.exampleCN: 这家动物园养着来自各大洲的动物。
senses.why: Since humans breathe too, English uses animal to draw the line between people and the rest of the living world.
senses.whyCN: 因为人也呼吸，英语便用 animal 划出人与其余生物之间的界线。

senses.title: Of animals or the body
senses.definition: relating to animals, or to the physical body rather than the mind or spirit
senses.definitionCN: 与动物有关的，或指肉体而非心智与精神
senses.example: Animal fat is solid at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 动物脂肪在室温下是固态的。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the old contrast with spirit: whatever is animal belongs to the body and its appetites.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了与精神相对的古义：属于动物性的东西归于肉体及其欲望。

intro.en: Animal is a Latin word for 'breathing being', and the breath inside it still shows in its relatives.
intro.cn: animal 是拉丁语中表示「有气息的存在」的词，其中的「气息」仍留在同族词里。

items.en: anima meant 'breath, air, soul', the principle that makes something alive.
items.cn: anima 意为「气息、空气、灵魂」，是使某物活着的本原。

items.en: animalis was the adjective meaning 'living, having breath'.
items.cn: animalis 是形容词，意为「活的、有气息的」。

items.en: The neuter noun animal meant 'a living being'.
items.cn: 中性名词 animal 意为「活物」。

items.en: French passed the noun to English with the sense 'living creature'.
items.cn: 法语把名词传给英语，义为「活物」。

items.en: English first used animal of any living thing, human beings included.
items.cn: 英语最初用 animal 指任何活物，包括人。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the everyday sense narrows to non-human creatures.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，日常用法中的词义收窄为指人以外的生物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for breath; the near-meaning group varies from general to collective.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「气息」的拉丁词根；近义组从泛指到集合名词依次排列。

entries.definition: to give life or liveliness to
wild animals taken as a group

normalIntro.en: Animal and animate are twins from Latin anima, 'breath'.
normalIntro.cn: animal 与 animate 是来自拉丁语 anima「气息」的一对同根词。

normal.en: Animal shares its root with animate: breath.
normal.cn: animal 与 animate 同根，核心是「气息」。

normal.en: A plant does not move or breathe; an animal does.
normal.cn: 植物不移动也不呼吸，动物则会。

normal.en: Animals is the regular plural, with no doubling.
normal.cn: 复数 animals 规则变化，不双写字母。

normal.en: As an adjective animal means bodily, as in animal fat.
normal.cn: 作形容词时 animal 指肉体的，如 animal fat。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-i-mal.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-i-mal。

abstract.en: See a cow lifting its head.
abstract.cn: 想象一头牛抬起头。

abstract.en: Hear slow breathing in a barn.
abstract.cn: 听到谷仓里缓慢的呼吸声。

abstract.en: Feel warm fur under your hand.
abstract.cn: 感到手下温热的皮毛。

examples.en: Every animal in the shelter needs a home.
examples.cn: 收容所里的每只动物都需要一个家。

examples.en: Some animals sleep through the whole winter.
examples.cn: 有些动物整个冬天都在睡眠中度过。

examples.en: The documentary shows animal behaviour in the wild.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片展示野外的动物行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: anima（气息、灵魂）加 -al（……的）：有气息的活物，动物。

root: 来自拉丁语 animal「活物」，由 anima「气息、灵魂」加名词词尾 -al 构成；同根词有 animate、animation、inanimate，词根始终围绕「气息、生命」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun separates creatures from plants and from people; the adjective points to the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 名词把动物与植物、与人区分开；形容词则指向肉体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cow raising its head in a field.
core.cn: 核心意象：田里抬头的一头牛。

intro.en: A Latin noun built on the root for breath, with a whole family of relatives.
intro.cn: 这是一个建立在「气息」词根上的拉丁名词，同族词众多。

latinIntro.en: The word comes straight from Latin, so the Latin items show the steps of its formation.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词直接来自拉丁语，因此拉丁词条列出它的构成步骤。

definition_zh: 踝；脚踝；踝部（衣物或水面达到的高度）
definition_en: the joint between the foot and the leg, or the narrow part of the leg just above the foot
core_image: 脚跟上方突出的那节骨节
scene: 他跳下台阶时脚一歪，痛得蹲了下去。She twisted her ankle on the icy steps.
sceneCN: 这里 ankle 是「脚踝」（第 1 个义项：脚与小腿相接的关节）；句意是她在结冰的台阶上扭伤了脚踝。

senses.title: The joint itself
senses.definition: the joint that connects the foot to the leg, where the leg narrows above the heel
senses.definitionCN: 连接脚与小腿的关节，位于脚跟上方小腿变窄处
senses.example: She twisted her ankle on the icy steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她在结冰的台阶上扭伤了脚踝。
senses.why: Ankle is a Germanic word for the bend of the leg, so it names the joint where the foot turns.
senses.whyCN: ankle 是日耳曼语中表示腿部弯折处的词，因此指脚转向的那个关节。

senses.title: The narrow part above the foot
senses.titleCN: 踝部（衣物或水达到的位置）
senses.definition: the narrow part of the leg just above the foot, used of clothing, socks, or the depth of water
senses.definitionCN: 脚上方小腿的狭窄部位，用于描述衣物、袜子或水的深度
senses.example: The water was ankle-deep after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后，水只没到脚踝那么深。
senses.why: Because the joint is the lowest narrow point of the leg, the same word measures how high socks, boots, or water reach.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个关节是腿部最低的窄处，同一个词便用来量袜子、靴子或水到达的高度。

intro.en: Ankle is an old Germanic word for the bend of the leg, and it is a distant cousin of angle.
intro.cn: ankle 是日耳曼语中表示腿部弯折处的老词，与 angle 是远亲。

items.en: ankulaz meant 'ankle', built on a root for 'bend, angle'.
items.cn: ankulaz 意为「踝」，由表示「弯折、角」的词根构成。

items.en: The Old English form anclēow already meant the ankle joint.
items.cn: 古英语形式 anclēow 已指踝关节。

items.en: The word shrank to ankle, losing its older ending.
items.cn: 这个词缩略为 ankle，失去了较早的词尾。

items.en: Ankle is recorded in the fourteenth century with its modern spelling.
items.cn: ankle 在十四世纪已有现代拼写的记录。

items.en: Compounds such as ankle socks and ankle-deep turn the joint into a measure of height.
items.cn: ankle socks 与 ankle-deep 等复合词把这个关节变成高度的量度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same bend-root; the near-meaning group holds other body joints.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「弯折」词根构成的词；近义组收其他身体关节。

entries.definition: a corner, or the space between two lines
a small ornament worn around the ankle
the joint between the hand and the arm
the back part of the foot
a place where two bones meet

normalIntro.en: Ankle and angle both go back to a word for a bend.
normalIntro.cn: ankle 与 angle 都上溯到表示「弯折」的词。

normal.en: Ankle and angle share the idea of a bend.
normal.cn: ankle 与 angle 共享「弯折」这一概念。

normal.en: Twist your ankle is the usual injury phrase.
normal.cn: twist your ankle 是常见的受伤说法。

normal.en: Ankles is the regular plural, with no doubling.
normal.cn: 复数 ankles 规则变化，不双写字母。

normal.en: Ankle socks stop right at the ankle.
normal.cn: ankle socks 正好停在脚踝处。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-kle.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-kle。

abstract.en: See the bone that stands out at the side of the foot.
abstract.cn: 想象脚外侧突出的那块骨。

abstract.en: Hear a sharp gasp after a bad step.
abstract.cn: 听到踩空后一声急促的抽气。

abstract.en: Feel ice under a thin sock.
abstract.cn: 感到薄袜下冰凉的台阶。

examples.en: He broke his ankle playing football.
examples.cn: 他踢球时摔断了脚踝。

examples.en: Her ankle was still swollen a week later.
examples.cn: 一周后她的脚踝仍然肿着。

examples.en: The path was ankle-deep in mud.
examples.cn: 小路上的泥没过了脚踝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 与 angle（角、弯折）同源：腿在脚上方弯折的那个关节，脚踝。

root: 来自古英语 anclēow，上溯原始日耳曼语 ankulaz，词根义为「弯折、弯曲」，与 angle（角）同源；指腿在脚上方弯折处的关节。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is the joint; the other measures how high something reaches on the leg.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项指关节本身，另一个义项量度某物在腿上达到的高度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bone that stands out above the heel.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚跟上方突出的骨节。

intro.en: A short native noun that forms compounds freely with clothing and depth words.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的本族名词，容易与衣物、深度类词构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic; the Latin cognate angulus appears only in the related word angle.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是日耳曼语；拉丁同源词 angulus 只出现在相关的 angle 中。

items.meaning: an ornament worn at the ankle

definition_zh: 周年纪念日；周年
definition_en: a date on which something is remembered each year, whether with celebration or with solemn ceremony
core_image: 日历翻回去年折过角的那一页
scene: 两个人坐在小餐馆靠窗的位置，桌上摆着一支点燃的蜡烛。They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in a small restaurant.
sceneCN: 这里 anniversary 是「周年纪念日」（第 1 个义项：值得庆祝的周年日期）；句意是他们在小餐馆庆祝结婚十周年。

senses.title: A yearly date of celebration
senses.definition: a date each year on which people celebrate something that began then, such as a wedding
senses.definitionCN: 每年到了某件事开始的那一天，人们为之庆祝的日期，如结婚纪念日
senses.example: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in a small restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在小餐馆庆祝结婚十周年。
senses.why: The Latin word joins annus 'year' and vertere 'to turn': the year turns back to the same date, and that return is the anniversary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语来源把 annus「年」与 vertere「转」合在一起：年转回同一天，这次回转就是 anniversary。

senses.title: A yearly date of remembrance
senses.definition: the same date each year used to remember a sad or serious event, often with a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 每年同一日期用于追忆悲伤或重大事件的日子，常伴以仪式
senses.example: The town held a service on the anniversary of the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇在洪水周年那天举行了纪念仪式。
senses.why: The return of the date does not care whether the event was happy, so the same word marks grief as well as joy.
senses.whyCN: 日期的回转并不区分事件的喜悲，因此同一个词既能标记欢乐，也能标记哀悼。

intro.en: Anniversary is a Latin compound meaning 'turning back every year'.
intro.cn: anniversary 是一个拉丁语复合词，意为「每年转回来」。

items.en: annus meant 'year', the base of annual and annuity as well.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，也是 annual 与 annuity 的词基。

items.en: vertere meant 'to turn', and the turning image survives in the word.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，转回的意象一直留在词里。

items.en: anniversarius meant 'returning every year', built from annus and vertere.
items.cn: anniversarius 意为「每年转回的」，由 annus 与 vertere 构成。

items.en: French passed the word into English with its religious sense intact.
items.cn: 法语把这个词传入英语，宗教纪念义随之而来。

items.en: English first used anniversary for a yearly religious observance.
items.cn: 英语最初用 anniversary 指每年的宗教纪念日。

items.en: From the seventeenth century it spread to weddings and then to any yearly date.
items.cn: 十七世纪起它扩展到婚礼，继而泛指任何周年日期。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin word for year; the near-meaning group covers other yearly markers.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「年」的词根；近义组是其他年度标记。

entries.definition: a fixed sum paid each year
the yearly date of one's birth
an act of honouring a person or event
a special anniversary marked with public celebration

normalIntro.en: Take annus 'year', add vertere 'turn', and you get the day the year turns back to.
normalIntro.cn: 取 annus「年」，加上 vertere「转」，得到的就是年转回的那一天。

normal.en: Anniversary joins the Latin words for year and turning.
normal.cn: anniversary 把拉丁语的「年」与「转」合在一起。

normal.en: The plural changes y to i: anniversaries.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 i：anniversaries。

normal.en: A wedding anniversary is the commonest use.
normal.cn: 结婚纪念日是最常见的用法。

normal.en: Say on the anniversary of, not in the anniversary of.
normal.cn: 要说 on the anniversary of，不用 in。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: an-ni-VER-sa-ry.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：an-ni-VER-sa-ry。

abstract.en: See a calendar page folding back to last year.
abstract.cn: 想象日历翻回去年折角的那一页。

abstract.en: See one candle on a small restaurant table.
abstract.cn: 想象小餐馆桌上一支点燃的蜡烛。

abstract.en: See a wreath laid at a memorial.
abstract.cn: 想象纪念碑前放下的花圈。

examples.en: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary in a small restaurant.
examples.cn: 他们在小餐馆庆祝结婚十周年。

examples.en: The town held a service on the anniversary of the flood.
examples.cn: 小镇在洪水周年那天举行了纪念仪式。

examples.en: Next month marks the anniversary of the museum's opening.
examples.cn: 下个月是博物馆开馆的周年纪念。

dict_mnemonic.text: ann（年）加 vers（转）加 -ary：一年转回一次的那天，周年纪念日。

root: 来自拉丁语 anniversarius「每年转回的」，由 annus「年」与 vertere「转」构成，经古法语 anniversaire 进入英语；核心义是「一年转回同一天」。

sensesIntro.en: Two uses: a happy yearly date and a solemn one.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种用法：喜庆的周年，与肃穆的周年纪念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar page turning back to the same date.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历翻回同一个日子。

intro.en: A Latin compound of 'year' and 'turn', with a small family of year-words around it.
intro.cn: 这是一个由「年」与「转」构成的拉丁语复合词，周围有一小族与年相关的词。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Latin, so the Latin items show how the compound was assembled.
latinIntro.cn: 两个词根都来自拉丁语，因此拉丁词条展示这个复合词是如何拼成的。

definition_zh: 宣布；通告；播报；预示
definition_en: to make something known officially and publicly, to read it out aloud, or to be a sign that something is coming
core_image: 麦克风前一张嘴向人群送出消息
scene: 会议室的门打开，负责人走上台，手里拿着一页纸。The company announced a new product on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 announce 是「宣布」（第 1 个义项：正式公开告知）；句意是公司在周一宣布了一款新产品。

pos.zh: 动词：宣布；通告；播报；预示

derivatives.zh: 名词：宣告，特指天使报喜

senses.title: To make known publicly
senses.definition: to tell people about a plan, decision, or fact in an official and public way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式、公开的方式把计划、决定或事实告诉众人
senses.example: The company announced a new product on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在周一宣布了一款新产品。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to bring news to', so the act is one of carrying a message from those who know to those who do not.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语动词意为「把消息带给」，因此这一动作就是把消息从知情者送到不知情者那里。

senses.title: To read out as a broadcaster
senses.definition: to read out names, times, or news aloud, as a broadcaster or official does
senses.definitionCN: 像播音员或工作人员那样，出声报出姓名、时间或消息
senses.example: The announcer announced the departure of the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 播音员播报了末班车的发车信息。
senses.why: Broadcasting turned the public statement into a spoken routine, so the same verb covers reading out a train time.
senses.whyCN: 广播把公开声明变成一种口头例行工作，于是同一个动词也用来报出列车时刻。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to make something clear by being a visible sign that it is coming
senses.definitionCN: 以可见的迹象说明某事即将到来
senses.example: The first buds announced the return of spring.
senses.exampleCN: 初生的嫩芽预示春天回来了。
senses.why: If news arrives before an event, then anything that arrives before an event can announce it, even a bud.
senses.whyCN: 如果消息先于事件到达，那么任何先于事件出现的东西都能 announce 它，哪怕只是一枚嫩芽。

intro.en: Announce carries the Latin word for a messenger inside it.
intro.cn: announce 里面藏着拉丁语表示「信使」的那个词。

items.en: nuntius meant 'messenger' and also 'message'.
items.cn: nuntius 既指「信使」，也指「消息」。

items.en: annuntiare meant 'to bring news to', built with ad- 'to'.
items.cn: annuntiare 意为「把消息带给」，由 ad-「向」构成。

items.en: French anoncer carried the word into English.
items.cn: 法语 anoncer 把这个词带入英语。

items.en: English announce first meant to proclaim something officially.
items.cn: 英语 announce 最初意为正式宣告某事。

items.en: Broadcasting added the sense of reading out names and times.
items.cn: 广播业增添了报出姓名与时间的义项。

items.en: The 'be a sign of' sense grows from news arriving before an event.
items.cn: 「预示」义来自消息先于事件到达这一想法。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the same messenger root; the near-meaning group differs in how public or forceful the statement is.
note.cn: 形近组共享「信使」词根；近义组按公开程度与语气强弱区分。

entries.definition: a person who reads out news or names
a formal announcement, especially a religious one
entries.definitionCN: 宣告，尤指宗教中的报喜

entries.definition: to state something firmly and officially
to make something previously hidden known
to make something known in order to sell it

normalIntro.en: Announce contains nounce, the same messenger idea as in nuncio.
normalIntro.cn: announce 里的 nounce 与 nuncio 一样，都是「信使、消息」的意思。

normal.en: The nounce in announce means messenger, as in nuncio.
normal.cn: announce 中的 nounce 意为信使，与 nuncio 同源。

normal.en: Announcement is the noun; announcer is the person.
normal.cn: announcement 是名词，announcer 指人。

normal.en: You announce news, never announce to news.
normal.cn: 要说 announce news，不说 announce to news。

normal.en: The past tense is announced, with no extra t.
normal.cn: 过去式是 announced，不要多加 t。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: an-NOUNCE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：an-NOUNCE。

abstract.en: See a hand steadying a microphone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶稳麦克风。

abstract.en: See a page of notes on a podium.
abstract.cn: 想象讲台上的一页讲稿。

abstract.en: See green buds opening on a bare branch.
abstract.cn: 想象光秃的枝条上绽开嫩芽。

examples.cn: 公司在周一宣布了一款新产品。

examples.en: The announcer announced the departure of the last train.
examples.cn: 播音员播报了末班车的发车信息。

examples.en: The first buds announced the return of spring.
examples.cn: 初生的嫩芽预示春天回来了。

dict_mnemonic.text: an-（向）加 nounce（消息、信使）：把消息送向大家，宣布。

root: 来自拉丁语 annuntiare「把消息带给」，由 ad-「向」与 nuntius「信使、消息」构成，经古法语 anoncer 进入英语；同根词有 announcement、announcer、annunciation。

sensesIntro.en: Three uses: public statements, broadcast reading, and signs of what is coming.
sensesIntro.cn: 三种用法：公开声明、广播播报，以及预示将来之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice at a microphone speaking to a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：麦克风前向人群说话的声音。

branches.en: announce the departure of a train

intro.en: A Latin verb of message-carrying, with a full set of derived nouns and one formal relative.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「传递消息」的拉丁语动词，派生名词齐全，还有一个正式的同族词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin nuntius, 'messenger', seen in all the items below.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 nuntius「信使」，下列词条都可见到它。

items.meaning: a person who reads out news

definition_zh: 使恼火；惹烦；（旧）骚扰、袭扰
definition_en: to make someone feel slightly angry, or, in older military use, to harass a place or force repeatedly
core_image: 一只关不掉、一直滴水的水龙头
scene: 楼上的音乐一遍遍重复同一段旋律，楼下的人合上了书。The constant noise from the flat above annoyed her.
sceneCN: 这里 annoy 是「使恼火」（第 1 个义项：让人心里生出轻微怒气）；句意是楼上不断的噪声让她恼火。

senses.title: To make someone slightly angry
senses.definition: to make a person feel slightly angry or irritated, usually by something repeated or small
senses.definitionCN: 使人心里生出轻微的怒气或不快，通常由反复出现的小事引起
senses.example: The constant noise from the flat above annoyed her.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上不断的噪声让她很恼火。
senses.why: The old French verb meant 'to trouble and weary', a weariness that the modern everyday sense keeps.
senses.whyCN: 这个古法语动词意为「使困扰、使厌倦」，现代日常义里仍保留着这种被磨出来的疲惫感。

senses.title: To harass, in older military use
senses.definition: to attack or trouble an enemy or a place repeatedly without a full battle
senses.definitionCN: 不进行正式会战，而反复袭扰敌人或某地
senses.example: Enemy patrols annoyed the column all night.
senses.exampleCN: 敌方巡逻队整夜袭扰这支行军纵队。
senses.why: The earliest English sense was to harm or molest, and military writing kept that harder meaning after everyday speech softened it.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项是伤害或侵扰，日常口语把词义软化之后，军事文本仍保留了这层更硬的意味。

intro.en: Annoy began with hatred, then softened into everyday irritation.
intro.cn: annoy 最初与憎恨有关，后来才软化为日常的烦躁。

items.en: odium meant 'hatred', the emotional core of the family.
items.cn: odium 意为「憎恨」，是这个词族的情感核心。

items.en: inodiare meant 'to make hateful', built with in- on odium.
items.cn: inodiare 意为「使可憎」，由 in- 加 odium 构成。

items.en: anuier meant 'to trouble, molest, weary'.
items.cn: anuier 意为「使困扰、侵扰、使厌倦」。

items.en: English annoy first meant to harm or molest.
items.cn: 英语 annoy 最初意为伤害或侵扰。

items.en: Everyday use keeps the milder sense; the military sense survives in older writing.
items.cn: 日常用法保留较温和的义项，军事义多见于较早的文本。

note.en: The look-alike group is the annoy family; the near-meaning group grades how strong or how repeated the irritation is.
note.cn: 形近组是 annoy 词族；近义组按恼人程度与反复程度分级。

entries.definition: a feeling of slight anger, or its cause
to disturb or trouble someone mildly
to keep troubling someone with requests

normalIntro.en: Annoy and annoyance share one short stem, with no doubling of the n.
normalIntro.cn: annoy 与 annoyance 共用一个短词干，n 不需要重复。

normal.en: Annoy keeps the same stem in annoyance.
normal.cn: annoy 在 annoyance 中词干不变。

normal.en: You are annoyed at a thing, annoyed with a person.
normal.cn: 对事用 annoyed at，对人用 annoyed with。

normal.en: The past tense is annoyed, with no doubled consonant.
normal.cn: 过去式是 annoyed，辅音不双写。

normal.en: Annoying describes the thing that annoys you.
normal.cn: annoying 形容那个惹你烦的东西。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: an-NOY.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：an-NOY。

abstract.en: Hear a tap dripping without stop.
abstract.cn: 听到水龙头不停地滴水。

abstract.en: See a fly beating against a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一只苍蝇在窗上乱撞。

abstract.en: Feel a phone buzzing again and again.
abstract.cn: 感到手机一遍遍震动。

examples.en: The constant noise from the flat above annoyed her.
examples.cn: 楼上不断的噪声让她很恼火。

examples.en: Stop annoying your sister while she is reading.
examples.cn: 你姐姐看书时别再烦她。

examples.en: Enemy patrols annoyed the column all night.
examples.cn: 敌方巡逻队整夜袭扰这支行军纵队。

dict_mnemonic.text: an-（使）加 noy（源自拉丁语「憎恨」）：让人心里生厌，惹恼。

root: 来自古法语 anuier「使困扰、侵扰」，上溯拉丁语 inodiare「使可憎」，由 in- 与 odium「憎恨」构成；英语最初意为伤害、侵扰，后缓和为「使烦恼」。

sensesIntro.en: One sense is everyday irritation; the other is the older military sense of harassing.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项是日常的惹恼，另一个是较早的军事义「袭扰」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping tap you cannot switch off.
core.cn: 核心意象：关不掉的水龙头在滴水。

intro.cn: 这是一个表示轻微烦躁的动词，名词与形容词形式都很规整。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is odium, 'hatred', still visible behind the French shape of the word.
